sentences.zh: 【魏紀十】起玄黓敦牂，盡瘀逢涒灘，凡三年。

translations.literal: [Wei Records 10] From Xuanyi Dunzang through Yufeng Tanyun, three years in all.
translations.idiomatic: [Records of Wei, Number Ten] Spanning from the cyclical year Xuanyi Dunzang through Yufeng Tanyun—three years in all.

sentences.zh: 元皇帝下景元三年（

translations.literal: Under Emperor Yuan, third year of Jingyuan (
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Yuan, third year of Jingyuan (

sentences.zh: 壬午，公元二六二年）

translations.literal: renwu, AD 262)
translations.idiomatic: the year renwu, AD 262)

sentences.zh: 秋，八月，乙酉，吳主立皇后朱氏，朱公主之女也。

translations.literal: In autumn, eighth month, day yiyou, the Lord of Wu installed Lady Zhu as empress; she was the daughter of Princess Zhu.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, in the eighth month, on the day yiyou, the Wu ruler established Lady Zhu as empress—she was a daughter of Princess Zhu.

sentences.zh: 戊子，立子為太子。

translations.literal: On day wuzi, he established his son as crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: On the day wuzi, he named his son crown prince.

sentences.zh: 漢大將軍姜維將出軍，右車騎將軍廖化曰：「兵不戢，必自焚，伯約之謂也。

translations.literal: Jiang Wei, Grand General of Han, was about to lead troops out; Right Chariots and Cavalry General Liao Hua said, "If troops are not kept in check, they will surely burn themselves up—this applies to Boyue.
translations.idiomatic: Grand General Jiang Wei of Shu was preparing to march when Right Chariots and Cavalry General Liao Hua warned, "Armies unchecked inevitably destroy themselves—this is precisely Boyue's situation.

sentences.zh: 智不出敵而力少於寇，用之無厭，將何以存！」

translations.literal: Your wisdom is to no advantage over the enemy, yet your strength is less than the invader's; if you use troops without restraint, how will you survive!"
translations.idiomatic: Your strategy cannot outmatch the foe, and your forces are weaker than the enemy's—if you keep deploying them without limit, how can the state endure?"

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，維入寇洮陽，鄧艾與戰於侯和，破之，維退住沓中。

translations.literal: In winter, tenth month, Wei invaded Taoyang; Deng Ai fought him at Houhe and defeated him; Wei withdrew and encamped at Tazhong.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, in the tenth month, Jiang Wei raided Taoyang. Deng Ai met him at Houhe and routed his army, forcing Jiang Wei to fall back and hold Tazhong.

sentences.zh: 初，維以羈旅依漢，身受重任，興兵累年，功績不立。

translations.literal: At the outset, Wei as a traveler in exile had relied on Han, bore heavy responsibility, raised troops for many years, yet achievements were not established.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Wei had come to Shu as an outsider in exile, entrusted with grave responsibilities; for years he had raised armies, yet achieved nothing.

sentences.zh: 黃皓用事於中，與右大將軍閻宇親善，陰欲廢維樹宇。

translations.literal: Huang Hao wielded power at court, was on close terms with Right Grand General Yan Yu, and secretly wished to remove Wei and install Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Hao held sway at court and was intimate with Right Grand General Yan Yu; secretly he sought to displace Jiang Wei and promote Yu in his place.

sentences.zh: 維知之，言於漢主曰：「皓奸巧專恣，將敗國家，請殺之！」

translations.literal: Wei knew this and said to the Lord of Han, "Hao is treacherous, cunning, and domineering; he will ruin the state—please put him to death!"
translations.idiomatic: Learning of this, Jiang Wei told the Shu ruler, "Huang Hao is treacherous, cunning, and utterly unrestrained—he will bring down the realm. I beg you to have him executed!"

sentences.zh: 漢主曰：「皓趨走小臣耳，往董允每切齒，吾常恨之，君何足介意！」

translations.literal: The Lord of Han said, "Hao is only a running attendant—formerly Dong Yun gnashed his teeth at him, which I always resented; why should you bother with such a man!"
translations.idiomatic: The Shu ruler replied, "Huang Hao is merely a palace runner. Dong Yun used to rail against him constantly, and I always resented that—why should a man of your stature trouble yourself over him?"

sentences.zh: 維見皓枝附葉連，懼於失言，遜辭而出，漢主敕皓詣維陳謝。

translations.literal: Wei saw that Hao had many branches and connections, feared a slip of the tongue, spoke deferentially and left; the Lord of Han ordered Hao to go to Wei and offer apologies.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Wei saw how deeply Huang Hao's influence had spread through the court and, fearing he had said too much, withdrew with polite excuses. The Shu ruler then commanded Huang Hao to visit Jiang Wei and offer his apologies.

sentences.zh: 維由是自疑懼，返自洮陽，因求種麥沓中，不敢歸成都。

translations.literal: From this Wei became wary and fearful; returning from Taoyang, he requested to plant wheat at Tazhong and did not dare return to Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: From that point Jiang Wei grew suspicious and afraid. On returning from Taoyang he asked permission to grow wheat at Tazhong and did not dare go back to Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 吳主以濮陽興為丞相，廷尉丁密、光祿勳孟宗為左右御史大夫。

translations.literal: The Lord of Wu appointed Puyang Xing as chancellor, and Court Commandant Ding Mi and Director of Imperial Banquets Meng Zong as left and right Censor-in-Chiefs.
translations.idiomatic: The Wu ruler made Puyang Xing chancellor and appointed Court Commandant Ding Mi and Director of Imperial Banquets Meng Zong as the Left and Right Censor-in-Chiefs.

sentences.zh: 初，興為會稽太守，吳主在會稽，興遇之厚；

translations.literal: At the outset, Xing had been governor of Kuaiji; when the Lord of Wu was at Kuaiji, Xing treated him generously;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Puyang Xing had served as governor of Kuaiji. When the Wu ruler was still there, Xing had treated him with great kindness.

sentences.zh: 左將軍張布嘗為會稽王左右督將，故吳主即位，二人皆貴寵用事；

translations.literal: Left General Zhang Bu had once been a supervising general to the King of Kuaiji; therefore when the Lord of Wu took the throne, both men were honored, favored, and wielded power;
translations.idiomatic: Left General Zhang Bu had once served as a supervising commander to the King of Kuaiji, so when the Wu ruler took the throne both men rose to favor and held real power.

sentences.zh: 布典宮省，興關軍國，以佞巧更相表裡，吳人失望。

translations.literal: Bu managed the palace and inner offices, Xing handled military and state affairs; through flattery and cunning they supported each other inside and out, and the people of Wu were disappointed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Bu controlled palace affairs while Puyang Xing handled military and state matters; through flattery and mutual collusion they ruled from within and without, and the people of Wu lost hope.

sentences.zh: 吳主喜讀書，欲與博士祭酒韋昭、博士盛沖講論，張布以昭、沖切直，恐其入侍，言己陰過，固諫止之。

translations.literal: The Lord of Wu enjoyed reading and wished to discuss and debate with Libationer of the Erudites Wei Zhao and Erudite Sheng Chong; Zhang Bu, because Zhao and Chong were blunt and upright, feared they would attend and speak of his hidden faults, and firmly remonstrated to stop it.
translations.idiomatic: The Wu ruler loved books and wished to hold discussions with Wei Zhao, Libationer of the Erudites, and Sheng Chong, an Erudite. Zhang Bu, knowing both men were blunt and upright, feared that if they attended court they would expose his secret misdeeds, and he vigorously urged the ruler not to admit them.

sentences.zh: 吳主曰：「孤之涉學，群書略遍，但欲與昭等講習舊聞，亦何所損！

translations.literal: The Lord of Wu said, "In my studies I have read nearly all the classics; I merely wish to review old learning with Zhao and the others—what harm is there in that!
translations.idiomatic: The Wu ruler said, "I have read widely across the classics; I only wish to review familiar learning with Zhao and the others—what harm could that do?

sentences.zh: 君特當恐昭等道臣下奸慝，故不欲令入耳。

translations.literal: You are simply afraid that Zhao and the others will speak of the wickedness of your subordinates, and so do not wish to let them reach my ears.
translations.idiomatic: You are simply afraid that Zhao and the others will speak of the wickedness of officials like you, and so you do not want them within my hearing.

sentences.zh: 如此之事，孤已自備之，不須昭等然後乃解也。」

translations.literal: Matters such as these I am already prepared for; I need not wait for Zhao and the others before I understand."
translations.idiomatic: I am already well aware of such matters; I do not need Zhao and the others to explain them to me."

sentences.zh: 布惶恐陳謝，且言懼妨政事。

translations.literal: Bu, in fear, offered apologies and also said he was afraid it would interfere with state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Bu, terrified, apologized and added that he feared such sessions would interfere with governance.

sentences.zh: 吳主曰：「王務、學業，其流各異，不相妨也。

translations.literal: The Lord of Wu said, "Royal duties and scholarly pursuits follow different courses and do not interfere with each other.
translations.idiomatic: The Wu ruler said, "State business and scholarly study follow different paths—they do not get in each other's way.

sentences.zh: 此無所為非，而君以為不宜，是以孤有所及耳。

translations.literal: There is nothing improper in this, yet you think it unsuitable—so I have some understanding of the matter.
translations.idiomatic: There is nothing improper in this, yet you say it should not be done—so I already see what is really going on.

sentences.zh: 不圖君今日在事更行此於孤也，良甚不取！」

translations.literal: I did not expect that today, while in office, you would act toward me in this way—it is truly unacceptable!"
translations.idiomatic: I never imagined that now, while holding office, you would treat me this way—it is truly deplorable!"

sentences.zh: 布拜表叩頭。

translations.literal: Bu submitted a memorial and kowtowed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Bu submitted a memorial and kowtowed in submission.

sentences.zh: 吳主曰：「聊相開悟耳，何至叩頭乎！

translations.literal: The Lord of Wu said, "I was merely offering a little enlightenment—why go so far as to kowtow!
translations.idiomatic: The Wu ruler said, "I was only trying to set you straight a little—why kowtow over that!

sentences.zh: 如君之忠誠，遠近所知，吾今日之巍巍，皆君之功也。

translations.literal: Loyalty such as yours is known far and near; my lofty position today is entirely your achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Loyalty such as yours is known far and wide; the exalted throne I hold today is entirely your doing.

sentences.zh: 《詩》云：『靡不有初，鮮克有終。』

translations.literal: The Odes say: 'There is hardly anything without a beginning, but few reach a good end.'
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Songs says, 'Few things lack a beginning, but few reach a good end.'

sentences.zh: 終之實難，君其終之！」

translations.literal: Finishing well is truly difficult—see that you finish well!"
translations.idiomatic: Finishing well is truly hard—see that you finish well!"

sentences.zh: 然吳主恐布疑懼，卒如布意，廢其講業，不復使昭等入。

translations.literal: Yet the Lord of Wu, fearing Bu's suspicion and alarm, ultimately did as Bu wished, abolished the lectures, and no longer allowed Zhao and the others to enter.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the Wu ruler, fearing Zhang Bu's anxiety, ultimately gave in to him, abandoned the scholarly sessions, and never again admitted Zhao and the others to court.

sentences.zh: 譙郡嵇康，文辭壯麗，好言老、莊而尚奇任俠，與陳留阮籍、籍兄子咸、河內山濤、河南向秀、琅邪王戎、沛人劉伶特相友善，號竹林七賢。

translations.literal: Ji Kang of Qiao Commandery had magnificent literary style, loved to speak of Laozi and Zhuangzi and admired the unconventional and chivalric; with Ruan Ji of Chenliu, Ji's nephew Ruan Xian, Shan Tao of Henei, Xiang Xiu of Henan, Wang Rong of Langye, and Liu Ling of Pei he was especially friendly, and they were called the Seven Sages of the Bamboo Grove.
translations.idiomatic: Ji Kang of Qiao Commandery wrote in a magnificent literary style, loved to discourse on Laozi and Zhuangzi, and admired the unconventional and chivalric. He was especially close to Ruan Ji of Chenliu, Ruan Ji's nephew Ruan Xian, Shan Tao of Henei, Xiang Xiu of Henan, Wang Rong of Langye, and Liu Ling of Pei; together they were known as the Seven Sages of the Bamboo Grove.

sentences.zh: 皆崇尚虛無，輕蔑禮法，縱酒昏酣，遺落世事。

translations.literal: All revered emptiness and nothingness, scorned ritual and law, indulged in wine until drunken stupor, and abandoned worldly affairs.
translations.idiomatic: They all revered emptiness and nothingness, scorned ritual and law, drank themselves into stupor, and turned their backs on worldly affairs.

sentences.zh: 阮籍為步兵校尉，其母卒，籍方與人圍棋，對者求止，籍留與決賭。

translations.literal: Ruan Ji was Commandant of Footsoldiers; when his mother died, Ji was in the middle of a game of weiqi; his opponent asked to stop, but Ji kept him to finish the wager.
translations.idiomatic: Ruan Ji served as Commandant of Footsoldiers. When his mother died, he was in the middle of a game of weiqi; his opponent asked to stop, but Ji insisted they play the match out.

sentences.zh: 既而飲酒二斗，舉聲一號，吐血數升，毀瘠骨立。

translations.literal: Then he drank two dou of wine, let out a single cry, vomited several sheng of blood, and wasted away until only bones remained.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward he drank two dou of wine, gave a single wailing cry, vomited several sheng of blood, and wasted away until he was little more than skin and bone.

sentences.zh: 居喪，飲酒無異平日。

translations.literal: During mourning he drank no differently from ordinary days.
translations.idiomatic: Throughout the mourning period he drank no differently than on ordinary days.

sentences.zh: 司隸校尉何曾惡之，面質籍於司馬昭座曰：「卿縱情、背禮、敗俗之人，今忠賢執政、綜核名實，若卿之曹，不可長也！」

translations.literal: Director of Retainers He Zeng detested him and, face to face, confronted Ji before Sima Zhao's seat, saying, "You are a man who indulges his passions, violates ritual, and corrupts custom; now that the loyal and worthy govern and examine names against reality, men of your sort cannot be allowed to flourish!"
translations.idiomatic: Director of Retainers He Zeng detested him and confronted him to his face before Sima Zhao, saying, "You are a man who indulges his passions, violates ritual, and corrupts public morals. Now that the loyal and worthy govern and names are matched to reality, men of your sort cannot be allowed to flourish!"

sentences.zh: 因謂昭曰：「公方以孝治天下，而聽阮籍以重哀飲酒食肉於公座，何以訓人！

translations.literal: He then said to Zhao, "Your Grace governs the realm through filial piety, yet you allow Ruan Ji to drink wine and eat meat during deep mourning in your presence—how can you instruct others!
translations.idiomatic: He then said to Zhao, "Your Grace governs the realm through filial piety, yet you allow Ruan Ji to drink wine and eat meat in deep mourning right before your seat—how can you instruct others!

sentences.zh: 宜擯之四裔，無令污染華夏。」

translations.literal: He should be cast out to the four borderlands and not allowed to pollute the Central Realm."
translations.idiomatic: He should be cast out to the four borderlands and not allowed to pollute the Central Realm."

sentences.zh: 昭愛籍才，常擁護之。

translations.literal: Zhao admired Ji's talent and always shielded him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao admired Ji's talent and always shielded him.

sentences.zh: 曾，夔之子也。

translations.literal: Zeng was the son of Kui.
translations.idiomatic: He Zeng was the son of He Kui.

sentences.zh: 阮咸素幸姑婢；

translations.literal: Ruan Xian had long favored his aunt's maid;
translations.idiomatic: Ruan Xian had long favored his aunt's maid servant;

sentences.zh: 姑將婢去，咸方對客，遽借客馬而追之，累騎而還。

translations.literal: When his aunt took the maid away, Xian was entertaining guests; he immediately borrowed a guest's horse to pursue them and returned riding double.
translations.idiomatic: When his aunt took the maid away, Xian was entertaining guests; he immediately borrowed a guest's horse to chase after them and returned riding double.

sentences.zh: 劉伶嗜酒，常乘鹿車，攜一壺酒，使人荷鍤隨之，曰：「死便埋我。」

translations.literal: Liu Ling was addicted to wine; he often rode in a deer cart carrying a pot of wine, with a man bearing a spade following him, saying, "When I die, just bury me."
translations.idiomatic: Liu Ling was addicted to wine. He often rode in a deer cart with a pot of wine, a servant carrying a spade following behind, saying, "When I die, just bury me."

sentences.zh: 當時士大夫皆以為賢，爭慕效之，謂之放達。

translations.literal: Contemporary gentlemen all regarded this as worthy and vied to emulate it, calling it free and unrestrained.
translations.idiomatic: Contemporary gentlemen all regarded such behavior as admirable and vied to emulate it, calling it free and unrestrained.

sentences.zh: 鐘會方有寵於司馬昭，聞嵇康名而造之，康箕踞而鍛，不為之禮。

translations.literal: Zhong Hui was then in favor with Sima Zhao; hearing Ji Kang's fame he went to visit him; Kang sat with legs spread while forging iron and did not observe the rites toward him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Hui was then in favor with Sima Zhao. Hearing of Ji Kang's renown, he went to visit him. Kang sat with legs spread while forging iron and showed him no courtesy.

sentences.zh: 會將去，康曰：「何所聞而來，何所見而去？」

translations.literal: As Hui was about to leave, Kang said, "What did you hear that made you come, and what did you see that makes you leave?"
translations.idiomatic: As Hui was about to leave, Kang asked, "What did you hear that made you come, and what did you see that makes you leave?"

sentences.zh: 會曰：「聞所聞而來，見所見而去！」

translations.literal: Hui said, "I came upon what I heard, and I leave upon what I saw!"
translations.idiomatic: Hui replied, "I came upon what I had heard, and I leave upon what I have seen!"

sentences.zh: 遂深銜之。

translations.literal: From this he bore a deep grudge.
translations.idiomatic: From that moment he nursed a deep grudge against him.

sentences.zh: 山濤為吏部郎，舉康自代。

translations.literal: Shan Tao was Director of the Ministry of Personnel and recommended Kang to succeed himself.
translations.idiomatic: Shan Tao served as Director of the Ministry of Personnel and recommended Kang to succeed him.

sentences.zh: 康與濤書，自說不堪流俗，而非薄湯、武。

translations.literal: Kang wrote to Tao, declaring himself unfit for worldly convention and disparaging Tang and Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Kang wrote to Shan Tao, declaring himself unfit for worldly convention and disparaging the sage-kings Tang and Wu.

sentences.zh: 昭聞而怒之。

translations.literal: Zhao heard of it and was angered.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhao heard of this, he was enraged.

sentences.zh: 康與東平呂安親善，安兄巽誣安不孝，康為證其不然。

translations.literal: Kang was on close terms with Lü An of Dongping; An's elder brother Xun falsely accused An of unfilial conduct, and Kang testified that this was not so.
translations.idiomatic: Kang was close to Lü An of Dongping. An's elder brother Xun falsely accused An of unfilial conduct, and Kang testified on his behalf that this was untrue.

sentences.zh: 會因譖「康嘗欲助毌丘儉，且安、康有盛名於世，而言論放蕩，害時亂教，宜因此除之。」

translations.literal: Hui took the opportunity to slander them, saying, "Kang once wished to aid Guanqiu Jian, and moreover An and Kang enjoy great fame in the world, yet their words are reckless, harm the age, and disorder teaching—they should be removed on this account."
translations.idiomatic: Hui seized the opportunity to slander them, saying, "Kang once sought to aid Guanqiu Jian, and moreover An and Kang enjoy great fame throughout the realm, yet their words are reckless, harm the age, and subvert public morals—they should be eliminated on this account."

sentences.zh: 昭遂殺安及康。

translations.literal: Zhao then executed An and Kang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao then had An and Kang executed.

sentences.zh: 康嘗詣隱者汲郡孫登，登曰：「子才多識寡，難乎免於今之世矣！」

translations.literal: Kang once visited the recluse Sun Deng of Ji Commandery; Deng said, "Sir, your talent is great but your understanding is small—you will hardly escape unscathed in the world of today!"
translations.idiomatic: Kang once visited the recluse Sun Deng of Ji Commandery. Deng told him, "Sir, your talent is great but your understanding is limited—you will hardly escape unscathed in the world of today!"

sentences.zh: 司馬昭患姜維數為寇，官騎路遺求為刺客入蜀，從事中郎荀勖曰：「明公為天下宰，宜杖正義以伐違貳，而以刺客除賊，非所以刑於四海也。」

translations.literal: Sima Zhao was troubled that Jiang Wei repeatedly raided as an invader; Palace Cavalry Officer Lu Yi requested to serve as an assassin entering Shu; Attendant Gentleman Xun Xu said, "Your Excellency is steward of the realm and should rely on righteousness to punish rebellion; to remove enemies by assassins is not how to set an example for the four seas."
translations.idiomatic: Sima Zhao was troubled that Jiang Wei repeatedly raided the borders. Palace Cavalry Officer Lu Yi volunteered to enter Shu as an assassin. Attendant Gentleman Xun Xu said, "Your Excellency is steward of the realm and should rely on righteousness to punish rebellion; removing enemies by assassination is not how to set an example for the four seas."

sentences.zh: 昭善之。

translations.literal: Zhao approved of this.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao approved of this view.

sentences.zh: 勖，爽之曾孫也。

translations.literal: Xu was the great-grandson of Shuang.
translations.idiomatic: Xun Xu was the great-grandson of Xun Shuang.

sentences.zh: 昭欲大舉伐漢，朝臣多以為不可，獨司隸校尉鐘會勸之。

translations.literal: Zhao wished to launch a major campaign against Han; most court ministers thought it impossible, but only Director of Retainers Zhong Hui urged it.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Zhao wished to launch a major campaign against Shu. Most court ministers thought it impossible, but Director of Retainers Zhong Hui alone urged it on.

sentences.zh: 昭諭眾曰：「自定壽春已來，息役六年，治兵繕甲，以擬二虜。

translations.literal: Zhao instructed the assembly, saying, "Since settling Shouchun, we have rested corvée labor for six years, trained troops and repaired armor, to prepare against the two barbarian foes.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Zhao addressed the assembly, saying, "Since the pacification of Shouchun we have rested corvée labor for six years, training troops and repairing armor to prepare against our two enemies.

sentences.zh: 今吳地廣大而下濕，攻之用功差難，不如先定巴蜀，三年之後，因順流之勢，水陸並進，此滅虢取虞之勢也。

translations.literal: Now Wu's territory is vast yet low and damp; attacking it would require much labor and be difficult; it is better first to secure Ba-Shu, and three years later, riding the downstream current, advance by land and water together—this is the strategy of destroying Guo to take Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Wu's territory is vast yet low and damp; attacking it would require enormous effort. It is better first to secure Ba-Shu, and three years later, riding the downstream current, advance by land and water together—this is the strategy of destroying Guo to take Yu.

sentences.zh: 計蜀戰士九萬，居守成都及備他境不下四萬，然則餘眾不過五萬。

translations.literal: It is calculated that Shu has ninety thousand fighting men; those garrisoning Chengdu and guarding other borders are no fewer than forty thousand; thus the remaining force is no more than fifty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Shu has some ninety thousand fighting men, but no fewer than forty thousand are garrisoned at Chengdu or guarding other borders—leaving no more than fifty thousand in the field.

sentences.zh: 今絆姜維於沓中，使不得東顧，直指駱谷，出其空虛之地以襲漢中，以劉禪之暗，而邊城外破，士女內震，其亡可知也。」

translations.literal: Now if we tie Jiang Wei down at Tazhong so he cannot look east, strike directly at Luogu, emerge from empty territory to raid Hanzhong, and with Liu Shan's dimness, the border cities broken from without and men and women shaken within, their fall can be foreseen."
translations.idiomatic: If we tie Jiang Wei down at Tazhong so he cannot look east, strike directly at Luogu, emerge from undefended territory to raid Hanzhong, and with Liu Shan's folly, the border cities broken from without and the people shaken within, their fall can be foreseen."

sentences.zh: 乃以鐘會為鎮西將軍，都督關中。

translations.literal: He then appointed Zhong Hui as General Who Guards the West and supervisor of Guanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: He then appointed Zhong Hui General Who Guards the West and put him in command of Guanzhong.

sentences.zh: 征西將軍鄧艾以為蜀未有釁，屢陳異議；

translations.literal: General Who Conquers the West Deng Ai believed Shu had given no cause for war and repeatedly offered dissenting views;
translations.idiomatic: General Who Conquers the West Deng Ai believed Shu had given no cause for war and repeatedly offered dissenting views;

sentences.zh: 昭使主簿師纂為艾司馬以諭之，艾乃奉命。

translations.literal: Zhao sent Registrar Shi Zuan to serve as Ai's Major to instruct him, and Ai then accepted the command.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Zhao sent Registrar Shi Zuan to serve as Ai's Major to instruct him, and Ai then accepted the command.

sentences.zh: 姜維表漢主：「聞鐘會治兵關中，欲規進取，宜並遣左右車騎張翼、廖化，督諸軍分護陽安關口及陰平之橋頭，以防未然。」

translations.literal: Jiang Wei memorialized the Lord of Han, saying, "I hear that Zhong Hui is training troops in Guanzhong and intends to advance; we should simultaneously dispatch Left and Right Chariots and Cavalry Zhang Yi and Liao Hua to supervise the armies in guarding Yang'an Pass and the bridgehead at Yinping, to guard against what has not yet happened."
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Wei memorialized the Shu ruler, saying, "I hear that Zhong Hui is training troops in Guanzhong and intends to advance. We should simultaneously dispatch Left and Right Chariots and Cavalry Zhang Yi and Liao Hua to supervise the armies in guarding Yang'an Pass and the bridgehead at Yinping, to guard against what has not yet happened."

sentences.zh: 黃皓信巫鬼，謂敵終不自致，啟漢主寢其事，群臣莫知。

translations.literal: Huang Hao trusted shamans and ghosts, saying the enemy would never come of themselves; he reported to the Lord of Han to shelve the matter, and the ministers knew nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Hao trusted shamans and ghosts and declared the enemy would never come on their own. He persuaded the Shu ruler to shelve the matter, and the ministers knew nothing of it.

sentences.zh: 元皇帝下景元四年（

translations.literal: Under Emperor Yuan, fourth year of Jingyuan (
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Yuan, fourth year of Jingyuan (

sentences.zh: 癸未，公元二六三年）

translations.literal: guiwei, AD 263)
translations.idiomatic: the year guiwei, AD 263)

sentences.zh: 春，二月，覆命司馬昭進爵位如前，又辭不受。

translations.literal: In spring, second month, an edict again ordered Sima Zhao to advance in rank as before, and again he declined to accept.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, in the second month, an edict again ordered Sima Zhao to advance in rank as before, and again he declined to accept.

sentences.zh: 吳交趾太守孫言胥貪暴，為百姓所患；

translations.literal: Sun Yanxu, governor of Jiaozhi in Wu, was greedy and violent and was a affliction to the people;
translations.idiomatic: Sun Yanxu, governor of Jiaozhi in Wu, was greedy and violent and was a scourge to the people;

sentences.zh: 會吳主遣察戰鄧荀至交趾，荀擅調孔爵三十頭送建業，民憚遠役，因謀作亂。

translations.literal: When the Lord of Wu sent Inspector of Warfare Deng Xun to Jiaozhi, Xun on his own authority requisitioned thirty peacocks to send to Jianye; the people feared distant corvée and therefore plotted rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: When the Wu ruler sent Inspector of Warfare Deng Xun to Jiaozhi, Xun on his own authority requisitioned thirty peacocks to send to Jianye. The people feared distant corvée and plotted rebellion.

sentences.zh: 夏，五月，郡吏呂興等殺言胥及荀，遣使來請太守及兵，九真、日南皆應之。

translations.literal: In summer, fifth month, district officials Lü Xing and others killed Yanxu and Xun, sent envoys requesting a governor and troops, and Jiuzhen and Rinan both responded.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, in the fifth month, district officials Lü Xing and others killed Yanxu and Xun, sent envoys requesting a governor and troops, and Jiuzhen and Rinan both rose in response.

sentences.zh: 詔諸軍大舉伐漢，遣征西將軍鄧艾督三萬餘人自狄道趣甘松、沓中，以連綴姜維；

translations.literal: An edict ordered the armies to launch a major campaign against Han; General Who Conquers the West Deng Ai was dispatched to command more than thirty thousand men from Didao toward Gansong and Tazhong to pin down Jiang Wei;
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered the armies to launch a major campaign against Shu. General Who Conquers the West Deng Ai was dispatched to command more than thirty thousand men from Didao toward Gansong and Tazhong to pin down Jiang Wei;

sentences.zh: 雍州刺史諸葛緒督三萬餘人自祁山趣武街橋頭，絕維歸路；

translations.literal: Inspector of Yong Province Zhuge Xu commanded more than thirty thousand men from Qishan toward Wujie Bridgehead to cut off Wei's route of return;
translations.idiomatic: Inspector of Yong Province Zhuge Xu commanded more than thirty thousand men from Qishan toward Wujie Bridgehead to cut off Jiang Wei's route of return;

sentences.zh: 鐘會統十餘萬眾分從斜谷、駱谷、子午谷趣漢中。

translations.literal: Zhong Hui commanded more than one hundred thousand troops advancing in separate columns through Xiegu, Luogu, and Ziwu Valley toward Hanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Hui commanded more than one hundred thousand troops advancing in separate columns through Xiegu, Luogu, and Ziwu Valley toward Hanzhong.

sentences.zh: 以廷尉衛瓘持節監艾、會軍事，行鎮西軍司。

translations.literal: Court Commandant Wei Guan was sent with credentials to supervise the military affairs of Ai and Hui, acting as Army Supervisor of the West.
translations.idiomatic: Court Commandant Wei Guan was sent with imperial credentials to supervise the military affairs of Ai and Hui, serving as Army Supervisor of the West.

sentences.zh: 瓘，覬之子也。

translations.literal: Guan was the son of Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Guan was the son of Wei Ji.

sentences.zh: 會過幽州刺史王雄之孫戎，問「計將安出？」

translations.literal: Hui passed by Wang Rong, grandson of Inspector of You Province Wang Xiong, and asked, "What plan will you offer?"
translations.idiomatic: Hui passed Wang Rong, grandson of Inspector of You Province Wang Xiong, and asked, "What plan do you propose?"

sentences.zh: 戎曰：「道家有言，『為而不恃。』

translations.literal: Rong said, "The Daoists say, 'Act yet do not rely on it.
translations.idiomatic: Rong replied, "The Daoists say, 'Act yet do not rely on it.

sentences.zh: 非成功難，保之難也。」

translations.literal: It is not success that is hard, but preserving it that is hard."
translations.idiomatic: It is not success that is hard, but preserving it that is hard."

sentences.zh: 或以問參相國軍事平原劉寔曰：「鐘、鄧其平蜀乎？」

translations.literal: Someone asked Liu Shi of Pingyuan, who assisted the Chancellor's military affairs, saying, "Will Zhong and Deng pacify Shu?"
translations.idiomatic: Someone asked Liu Shi of Pingyuan, who assisted the Chancellor's military affairs, "Will Zhong and Deng pacify Shu?"

sentences.zh: 寔曰：「破蜀必矣，而皆不還。」

translations.literal: Shi said, "They will surely break Shu, but none will return."
translations.idiomatic: Liu Shi replied, "They will surely conquer Shu, but none of them will return."

sentences.zh: 客問其故，寔笑而不答。

translations.literal: The guest asked the reason; Shi smiled and did not answer.
translations.idiomatic: When asked why, Liu Shi smiled and did not answer.

sentences.zh: 秋，八月，軍發洛陽，大賚將士，陳師誓眾。

translations.literal: In autumn, eighth month, the army set out from Luoyang; the generals and soldiers were richly rewarded, and the troops were arrayed and sworn before the host.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, in the eighth month, the army set out from Luoyang. The generals and soldiers were richly rewarded, and the troops were arrayed and sworn before the host.

sentences.zh: 將軍鄧敦謂蜀未可討，司馬昭斬以徇。

translations.literal: General Deng Dun said Shu could not yet be attacked; Sima Zhao executed him as a warning.
translations.idiomatic: General Deng Dun said Shu could not yet be attacked. Sima Zhao had him executed as a warning to others.

sentences.zh: 漢人聞魏兵且至，乃遣廖化將兵詣沓中，為姜維繼援，張翼、董厥等詣陽安關口，為諸圍外助。

translations.literal: When the people of Han heard that Wei troops were about to arrive, they dispatched Liao Hua to lead troops to Tazhong to reinforce Jiang Wei, and Zhang Yi, Dong Jue, and others to Yang'an Pass to aid the outer encirclements.
translations.idiomatic: When the Shu court heard that Wei troops were approaching, it dispatched Liao Hua to lead troops to Tazhong to reinforce Jiang Wei, and Zhang Yi, Dong Jue, and others to Yang'an Pass to aid the outer encirclements.

sentences.zh: 大赦，改元炎興。

translations.literal: A general amnesty was proclaimed and the era name changed to Yanxing.
translations.idiomatic: A general amnesty was proclaimed and the era name was changed to Yanxing.

sentences.zh: 敕諸圍皆不得戰，退保漢、樂二城，城中各有兵五千人。

translations.literal: An order was issued that all encirclements must not give battle but withdraw to hold the two cities of Han and Le; each city had five thousand troops.
translations.idiomatic: An order was issued that all encirclements must not give battle but withdraw to hold the two cities of Han and Le, each garrisoned with five thousand troops.

sentences.zh: 翼、厥北至陰平，聞諸葛緒將向建威，留住月餘待之。

translations.literal: Yi and Jue went north to Yinping; hearing that Zhuge Xu was heading toward Jianwei, they halted for more than a month waiting for him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yi and Dong Jue went north to Yinping. Hearing that Zhuge Xu was heading toward Jianwei, they halted for more than a month waiting for him.

sentences.zh: 鐘會率諸軍平行至漢中。

translations.literal: Zhong Hui led the armies in parallel advance to Hanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Hui led the armies in parallel columns to Hanzhong.

sentences.zh: 九月，鐘會使前將軍李輔統萬人圍王含於樂城，護軍荀愷圍蔣斌於漢城。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, Zhong Hui sent Forward General Li Fu to command ten thousand men to besiege Wang Han at Lecheng, and Protector of the Army Xun Kai to besiege Jiang Bin at Hancheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, Zhong Hui sent Forward General Li Fu with ten thousand men to besiege Wang Han at Lecheng, and Protector of the Army Xun Kai to besiege Jiang Bin at Hancheng.

sentences.zh: 會徑過西趣陽安口，遺人祭諸葛亮墓。

translations.literal: Hui passed directly west toward Yang'an Pass and sent men to offer sacrifice at Zhuge Liang's tomb.
translations.idiomatic: Hui passed directly west toward Yang'an Pass and sent men to offer sacrifice at Zhuge Liang's tomb.

sentences.zh: 初，漢武興督蔣舒在事無稱，漢朝令人代之，使助將軍傅僉守關口，舒由是恨。

translations.literal: At the outset, Jiang Shu, supervisor of Wuxing in Han, had no distinction in office; the Han court sent someone to replace him and made Assistant General Fu Qian guard the pass; from this Shu bore resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Jiang Shu, supervisor of Wuxing in Shu, had distinguished himself in no way. The Shu court sent someone to replace him and made Assistant General Fu Qian guard the pass; from this Jiang Shu bore a grudge.

sentences.zh: 鐘會使護軍胡烈為前鋒，攻關口。

translations.literal: Zhong Hui made Protector of the Army Hu Lie the vanguard to attack the pass.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Hui made Protector of the Army Hu Lie the vanguard to attack the pass.

sentences.zh: 舒詭謂僉曰：「今賊至不擊而閉城自守，非良圖也。」

translations.literal: Shu deceitfully said to Qian, "Now that the enemy has arrived, not striking but closing the city to defend is not a good plan."
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Shu deceitfully said to Fu Qian, "Now that the enemy has arrived, to close the gates and defend without fighting is no good plan."

sentences.zh: 僉曰：「受命保城，惟全為功；

translations.literal: Qian said, "I received orders to defend the city; the only achievement is to preserve it intact;
translations.idiomatic: Fu Qian replied, "I received orders to defend this city, and my only duty is to preserve it intact.

sentences.zh: 今違命出戰，若喪師負國，死無益矣。」

translations.literal: If I disobey orders and go out to battle, and if I lose the army and fail the state, death would be of no benefit."
translations.idiomatic: If I disobey orders and go out to fight, and lose the army and fail the state, death would serve no purpose."

sentences.zh: 舒曰：「子以保城獲全為功，我以出戰克敵為功，請各行其志。」

translations.literal: Shu said, "You take preserving the city and achieving safety as your achievement; I take going out to battle and defeating the enemy as mine—please each follow your own intent."
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Shu said, "You take preserving the city as your achievement; I take going out to battle and defeating the enemy as mine. Let each of us follow his own intent."

sentences.zh: 遂率其眾出。

translations.literal: He then led his troops out.
translations.idiomatic: He then led his troops out.

sentences.zh: 僉謂其戰也，不設備。

translations.literal: Qian thought he was going out to fight and did not set up defenses.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Qian thought Jiang Shu was going out to fight and did not set up defenses.

sentences.zh: 舒率其眾迎降胡烈，烈乘虛襲城，僉格鬥而死，僉，肜之子也。

translations.literal: Shu led his troops out to welcome Hu Lie and surrender; Lie seized the opportunity to raid the city; Qian fought and died—Qian was the son of Rong.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Shu led his troops out to welcome Hu Lie and surrender. Lie seized the opportunity to raid the city. Fu Qian fought to the death—Fu Qian was the son of Fu Rong.

sentences.zh: 鐘會聞關口已下，長驅而前，大得庫藏積穀。

translations.literal: Hui heard the pass had fallen and drove straight forward, greatly obtaining stored treasures and accumulated grain.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhong Hui heard the pass had fallen, he drove straight forward and seized great stores of treasure and grain.

sentences.zh: 鄧艾遣天水太守王頎直攻姜維營，隴西太守牽弘邀其前，金城太守楊欣趣甘松。

translations.literal: Ai dispatched Tianshui Governor Wang Qi to strike directly at Jiang Wei's camp; Longxi Governor Qian Hong intercepted him from the front; Jincheng Governor Yang Xin hastened toward Gansong.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Ai dispatched Tianshui Governor Wang Qi to strike directly at Jiang Wei's camp, Longxi Governor Qian Hong to intercept him from the front, and Jincheng Governor Yang Xin to hasten toward Gansong.

sentences.zh: 維聞鐘會諸軍已入漢中，引兵還。

translations.literal: Wei heard that Zhong Hui's armies had entered Hanzhong and withdrew his troops.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Wei heard that Zhong Hui's armies had entered Hanzhong and withdrew his troops.

sentences.zh: 欣等追躡於強川口，大戰，維敗走。

translations.literal: Xin and the others pursued at Qiangchuan Pass; after a great battle Wei was defeated and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Xin and the others pursued him to Qiangchuan Pass. After a great battle Jiang Wei was defeated and fled.

sentences.zh: 聞諸葛緒已塞道屯橋頭，乃從孔函谷入北道，欲出緒後；

translations.literal: Hearing that Zhuge Xu had blocked the road and encamped at Bridgehead, he entered the northern route through Konghan Valley, intending to emerge behind Xu;
translations.idiomatic: Hearing that Zhuge Xu had blocked the road and encamped at Bridgehead, he entered the northern route through Konghan Valley, intending to emerge behind Xu.

sentences.zh: 緒聞之，卻還三十里。

translations.literal: Xu heard of this and withdrew thirty li.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhuge Xu heard of this, he withdrew thirty li.

sentences.zh: 維入北道三十餘里，聞緒軍卻，尋還，從橋頭還，緒趣截維，較一日不及。

translations.literal: Wei entered the northern route for more than thirty li; hearing Xu's army had withdrawn, he soon returned, going back from Bridgehead; Xu hurried to intercept Wei but was a day too late.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Wei advanced more than thirty li along the northern route, then hearing that Xu's army had withdrawn, turned back along the Bridgehead road. Xu hurried to intercept him but was a day too late.

sentences.zh: 維遂還至陰平，合集士眾，欲赴關城；

translations.literal: Wei then returned to Yinping, gathered troops, and wished to go to Guan City;
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Wei then returned to Yinping, gathered his forces, and intended to march to Guan City.

sentences.zh: 未到，聞其已破，退趣白水，遇廖化、張翼、董厥等，合兵守劍閣以拒會。

translations.literal: Before arriving he heard it had fallen; he retreated toward Baishui, met Liao Hua, Zhang Yi, Dong Jue and others, combined forces and held Jian'ge Pass to resist Hui.
translations.idiomatic: Before he arrived he heard it had already fallen. He retreated toward Baishui, met Liao Hua, Zhang Yi, Dong Jue, and others, combined their forces, and held Jian'ge Pass to resist Zhong Hui.

sentences.zh: 安國元侯高柔卒。

translations.literal: Marquis Yuan of Anguo Gao Rou died.
translations.idiomatic: Marquis Yuan of Anguo, Gao Rou, died.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，漢人告急於吳。

translations.literal: In winter, tenth month, the people of Han reported urgency to Wu.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, in the tenth month, the Shu court sent urgent appeals for help to Wu.

sentences.zh: 甲申，吳主使大將軍丁奉督諸軍向壽春；

translations.literal: On day jiashen, the Lord of Wu sent Grand General Ding Feng to supervise the armies toward Shouchun;
translations.idiomatic: On the day jiashen, the Wu ruler sent Grand General Ding Feng to supervise the armies toward Shouchun.

sentences.zh: 將軍留平就施績於南郡，議兵所向；

translations.literal: General Liu Ping joined Shi Ji at Nan Commandery to discuss where the armies should be directed;
translations.idiomatic: General Liu Ping joined Shi Ji at Nan Commandery to discuss where the armies should be directed.

sentences.zh: 將軍丁封、孫異如沔中，以救漢。

translations.literal: Generals Ding Feng and Sun Yi went to the Mian region to rescue Han.
translations.idiomatic: Generals Ding Feng and Sun Yi marched into the Mian region to rescue Shu.

sentences.zh: 詔以征蜀諸將獻捷交至，覆命大將軍昭進位，爵賜一如前詔，昭乃受命。

translations.literal: An edict, because the generals campaigning against Shu reported victory after victory, again ordered Grand General Zhao to advance in rank; titles and gifts were as in the previous edict, and Zhao then accepted.
translations.idiomatic: Because the generals campaigning against Shu reported victory after victory, an edict again ordered Grand General Zhao to advance in rank with titles and gifts as in the previous edict, and Zhao accepted.

sentences.zh: 昭辟任城魏舒為相國參軍。

translations.literal: Zhao recruited Wei Shu of Rencheng as military adviser to the Chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Zhao recruited Wei Shu of Rencheng as military adviser to the Chancellor.

sentences.zh: 初，舒少時遲鈍質樸，不為鄉親所重，從叔父事部郎衡，有名當世，亦不知之，使守水碓，每歎曰；

translations.literal: At the outset, in youth Shu was slow, dull, and plain, not esteemed by kinsmen and neighbors; his father's younger brother served Section Chief Heng, famous in the age, yet did not know Shu's worth and made him guard the water mill, sighing each time:
translations.idiomatic: In his youth Wei Shu was slow, dull, and plain, and was not esteemed by kinsmen and neighbors. His father's younger brother served Section Chief Heng, a man famous in his day, yet even he failed to recognize Shu's worth and made him guard the water mill, sighing each time:

sentences.zh: 「舒堪數百戶長，我願畢矣！」

translations.literal: "Shu is fit to be head of a few hundred households—that is all I can wish for him!"
translations.idiomatic: "Shu is fit to be headman of a few hundred households—that is all I can hope for him!"

sentences.zh: 舒亦不以介意，不為皎厲之事。

translations.literal: Shu also did not take it to heart and did not do sharp or aggressive things.
translations.idiomatic: Shu did not take this to heart and did not make a show of sharp or aggressive behavior.

sentences.zh: 唯太原王乂謂舒曰：「卿終當為台輔。」

translations.literal: Only Wang Yi of Taiyuan said to Shu, "Sir, you will ultimately become a pillar of the state."
translations.idiomatic: Only Wang Yi of Taiyuan told him, "Sir, you will one day become a pillar of the state."

sentences.zh: 常振其匱乏，舒受而不辭。

translations.literal: He often supplied Shu when he was in want; Shu accepted without declining.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yi often supplied Shu when he was in want, and Shu accepted without declining.

sentences.zh: 年四十餘，郡舉上計掾，察孝廉。

translations.literal: When he was over forty, the commandery recommended him as Chief Clerk for Tribute Accounts and nominated him as Filial and Incorrupt.
translations.idiomatic: When he was over forty, the commandery recommended him as Chief Clerk for Tribute Accounts and nominated him as Filial and Incorrupt.

sentences.zh: 宗黨以舒無學業，勸令不就，可以為高。

translations.literal: Clansmen, because Shu had no scholarly training, urged him not to accept, saying this could be taken as lofty.
translations.idiomatic: His clansmen, knowing he had no scholarly training, urged him not to accept, saying he could take the high ground by declining.

sentences.zh: 舒曰：「若試而不中，其負在我，安可虛竊不就之高以為己榮乎！」

translations.literal: Shu said, "If I am tested and fail, the fault is mine—how can I falsely steal the loftiness of not accepting as my own glory!"
translations.idiomatic: Shu said, "If I am tested and fail, the fault is mine. How can I falsely claim the glory of declining without even trying!"

sentences.zh: 於是自課，百日習一經，因而對策升第，累遷後將軍鐘毓長史。

translations.literal: Thereupon he set himself to study, mastering one classic every hundred days; thus in the palace examination he passed and advanced, and was repeatedly promoted to Chief Clerk under Rear General Zhong Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he set himself to study, mastering one classic every hundred days. He passed the palace examination and rose through the ranks to become Chief Clerk under Rear General Zhong Yu.

sentences.zh: 毓每與參佐射，舒常為畫籌而已；

translations.literal: Whenever Yu played pitch-pot with his aides, Shu usually only drew the tally marks;
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Zhong Yu played pitch-pot with his aides, Shu usually only kept the tally marks.

sentences.zh: 後遇朋人不足，以舒滿數，舒容範閑雅，發無不中，舉坐愕然，莫有敵者。

translations.literal: Later when there were not enough companions, Shu was counted to fill the number; his bearing was dignified and leisurely, every throw hit, and the whole company was astonished—none could match him.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when there were not enough players, Shu was counted to fill the number. His bearing was dignified and leisurely, every throw hit its mark, and the whole company was astonished—none could match him.

sentences.zh: 毓歎而謝曰：「吾之不足以盡卿才，有如此射矣，豈一事哉！」

translations.literal: Yu sighed and apologized, saying, "I was not sufficient to exhaust your talent—if this is how you pitch, is it only in one thing!"
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Yu sighed and apologized, saying, "I failed to recognize the full extent of your talent. If this is how you pitch, is your skill limited to one thing alone!"

sentences.zh: 及為相國參軍，府朝碎務，未嘗見是非；

translations.literal: When he became military adviser to the Chancellor, amid the trivial affairs of the office he was never seen to judge right and wrong;
translations.idiomatic: When he became military adviser to the Chancellor, amid the trivial affairs of the office he was never seen to pronounce on right and wrong.

sentences.zh: 至於廢興大事，眾人莫能斷者，舒徐為籌之，多出眾議之表。

translations.literal: But in great matters of rise and fall that the assembly could not decide, Shu would slowly work them out, and his conclusions often exceeded what the crowd had debated.
translations.idiomatic: But in great matters of rise and fall that the assembly could not decide, Shu would slowly work them out, and his conclusions often surpassed what the crowd had debated.

sentences.zh: 昭深器重之。

translations.literal: Zhao deeply valued and relied on him.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Zhao deeply valued and relied on him.

sentences.zh: 癸卯，立皇后卞氏，昭烈將軍秉之孫也。

translations.literal: On day guimao, Lady Bian was established as empress; she was the granddaughter of General Zhaolie Bing.
translations.idiomatic: On the day guimao, Lady Bian was established as empress—she was the granddaughter of General Zhaolie Bing.

sentences.zh: 鄧艾進至陰平，簡選精銳，欲與諸葛緒自江油趣成都。

translations.literal: Ai advanced to Yinping, selected elite troops, and wished with Zhuge Xu to go from Jiangyou toward Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Ai advanced to Yinping, selected elite troops, and intended to march with Zhuge Xu from Jiangyou toward Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 緒以本受節度邀姜維，西行非本詔，遂引軍向白水，與鐘會合。

translations.literal: Xu, because he had originally received orders to intercept Jiang Wei, held that marching west was not his original commission; he therefore led his army toward Baishui and joined Zhong Hui.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Xu, having originally received orders to intercept Jiang Wei, held that marching west was not part of his commission. He therefore led his army toward Baishui and joined Zhong Hui.

sentences.zh: 會欲專軍勢，密白緒畏懦不進，檻車征還，軍悉屬會。

translations.literal: Hui wished to monopolize military power; he secretly reported that Xu was cowardly and would not advance, had him recalled in a caged cart, and all troops came under Hui.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Hui wished to monopolize military power. He secretly reported that Zhuge Xu was cowardly and would not advance, had him recalled in a caged cart, and placed all troops under his own command.

sentences.zh: 姜維列營守險，會攻之，不能克；

translations.literal: Jiang Wei arrayed camps to hold the defiles; Hui attacked but could not overcome them;
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Wei arrayed camps to hold the defiles. Zhong Hui attacked but could not overcome them.

sentences.zh: 糧道險遠，軍食乏，欲引還。

translations.literal: The supply route was perilous and distant, army provisions were exhausted, and he wished to withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: The supply route was perilous and distant, army provisions were exhausted, and he wished to withdraw.

sentences.zh: 鄧艾上言：「賊已摧折，宜遂乘之。

translations.literal: Ai memorialized, saying, "The enemy is already broken—we should press the advantage at once.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Ai memorialized, saying, "The enemy is already broken—we should press the advantage at once.

sentences.zh: 若從陰平由邪徑經漢德陽亭趣涪，出劍閣西百里，去成都三百餘里，奇兵沖其腹心，出其不意，劍閣之守必還赴涪，則會方軌而進，劍閣之軍不還，則應涪之兵寡矣。」

translations.literal: If from Yinping we take the bypath through Hande Yangting toward Fu, emerging a hundred li west of Jian'ge and more than three hundred li from Chengdu, a surprise force strikes their vitals unexpectedly—the Jian'ge garrison will surely return to Fu, then Hui can advance on the main road; if the Jian'ge army does not return, the troops at Fu will be few."
translations.idiomatic: If we take the bypath from Yinping through Hande Yangting toward Fu, emerging a hundred li west of Jian'ge and more than three hundred li from Chengdu, a surprise force can strike their vitals unexpectedly. The Jian'ge garrison will surely return to Fu, and then Zhong Hui can advance on the main road. If the Jian'ge army does not return, the troops at Fu will be too few to resist."

sentences.zh: 遂自陰平行無人之地七百餘里，鑿山通道，造作橋閣。

translations.literal: He then marched from Yinping through uninhabited territory for more than seven hundred li, cutting through mountains to open paths and building bridges and galleries.
translations.idiomatic: He then marched from Yinping through uninhabited territory for more than seven hundred li, cutting through mountains to open paths and building bridges and galleries.

sentences.zh: 山高谷深，至為艱險，又糧運將匱，瀕於危殆。

translations.literal: Mountains were high and valleys deep, the route extremely perilous, and grain transport was nearly exhausted—they were on the brink of disaster.
translations.idiomatic: The mountains were high and the valleys deep, the route was extremely perilous, and grain transport was nearly exhausted—they were on the brink of disaster.

sentences.zh: 艾以氈自裹，推轉而下。

translations.literal: Ai wrapped himself in felt and rolled down.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Ai wrapped himself in felt and rolled down the slope.

sentences.zh: 將士皆攀木緣崖，魚貫而進。

translations.literal: Officers and soldiers all climbed trees and scaled cliffs, advancing in single file like fish through a weir.
translations.idiomatic: Officers and soldiers all climbed trees and scaled cliffs, advancing in single file like fish through a weir.

sentences.zh: 先登至江油，蜀守將馬邈降。

translations.literal: The vanguard reached Jiangyou; Shu defending general Ma Miao surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: The vanguard reached Jiangyou, and Shu's defending general Ma Miao surrendered.

sentences.zh: 諸葛瞻督諸軍拒艾，至涪，停住不進。

translations.literal: Zhuge Zhan supervised the armies resisting Ai; reaching Fu, he halted and did not advance.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Zhan supervised the armies resisting Deng Ai. Reaching Fu, he halted and did not advance.

sentences.zh: 尚書郎黃崇，權之子也，屢勸瞻宜速行據險，無令敵得入平地，瞻猶豫未納；

translations.literal: Attendant Gentleman Huang Chong, son of Quan, repeatedly urged Zhan to move quickly and hold the defiles, not letting the enemy enter flat ground; Zhan hesitated and did not accept;
translations.idiomatic: Attendant Gentleman Huang Chong, son of Huang Quan, repeatedly urged Zhuge Zhan to move quickly and hold the defiles, not letting the enemy reach flat ground. Zhuge Zhan hesitated and did not accept the advice.

sentences.zh: 崇再三言之，至於流涕，瞻不能從。

translations.literal: Chong spoke again and again until he wept; Zhan could not follow him.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Chong spoke again and again until he wept, but Zhuge Zhan would not listen.

sentences.zh: 艾遂長驅而前，擊破瞻前鋒，瞻退往綿竹。

translations.literal: Ai then drove straight forward, defeated Zhan's vanguard, and Zhan withdrew toward Mianzhu.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Ai then drove straight forward, defeated Zhuge Zhan's vanguard, and Zhuge Zhan withdrew toward Mianzhu.

sentences.zh: 艾以書誘瞻曰：「若降者，必表為琅邪王。」

translations.literal: Ai sent a letter to entice Zhan, saying, "If you surrender, I will surely memorialize to have you made King of Langye."
translations.idiomatic: Deng Ai sent a letter to entice Zhuge Zhan, saying, "If you surrender, I will surely memorialize to have you made King of Langye."

sentences.zh: 瞻怒，斬艾使，列陣以待艾。

translations.literal: Zhan was enraged, executed Ai's envoy, and arrayed his ranks to await Ai.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Zhan was enraged, executed Deng Ai's envoy, and arrayed his ranks to await him.

sentences.zh: 艾遣子惠唐亭候忠等出其右，司馬師纂等出其左。

translations.literal: Ai dispatched his son Zhong, Marquis of Huitangting, and others to emerge on their right, and Major Shi Zuan and others on their left.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Ai dispatched his son Deng Zhong, Marquis of Huitangting, and others to emerge on their right, and Major Shi Zuan and others on their left.

sentences.zh: 忠、纂戰不利，並引還，曰：「賊未可擊！」

translations.literal: Zhong and Zuan fought without success and both withdrew, saying, "The enemy cannot be attacked!"
translations.idiomatic: Deng Zhong and Shi Zuan fought without success and both withdrew, saying, "The enemy cannot be attacked!"

sentences.zh: 艾怒曰：「存亡之分，在此一舉，何不可之有！」

translations.literal: Ai angrily said, "The line between survival and destruction hangs on this one move—how can there be anything that cannot be done!"
translations.idiomatic: Deng Ai angrily said, "The line between survival and destruction hangs on this one move—how can there be anything that cannot be done!"

sentences.zh: 叱忠、纂等，將斬之。

translations.literal: He rebuked Zhong, Zuan, and the others and was about to execute them.
translations.idiomatic: He rebuked Deng Zhong, Shi Zuan, and the others and was about to execute them.

sentences.zh: 忠、纂馳還更戰，大破，斬瞻及黃崇。

translations.literal: Zhong and Zuan galloped back to fight again; they won a great victory and beheaded Zhan and Huang Chong.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Zhong and Shi Zuan galloped back to fight again. They won a great victory and beheaded Zhuge Zhan and Huang Chong.

sentences.zh: 瞻子尚歎曰：「父子荷國重恩，不早斬黃皓，使敗國殄民，用生何為！」

translations.literal: Zhan's son Shang sighed, saying, "Father and son have received the state's heavy grace; we did not early behead Huang Hao, letting the state fall and the people perish—what use is living!"
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Zhan's son Zhuge Shang sighed, saying, "Father and son have received the state's heavy grace. We did not behead Huang Hao in time, letting the state fall and the people perish—what use is living!"

sentences.zh: 策馬冒陣而死。

translations.literal: He spurred his horse into the enemy ranks and died.
translations.idiomatic: He spurred his horse into the enemy ranks and died.

sentences.zh: 漢人不意魏兵卒至，不為城守調度；

translations.literal: The people of Han did not expect Wei troops to arrive so suddenly and made no arrangements for city defense;
translations.idiomatic: The people of Shu did not expect Wei troops to arrive so suddenly and made no arrangements for city defense.

sentences.zh: 聞艾已入平土，百姓擾擾，皆迸山野，不可禁制。

translations.literal: Hearing that Ai had entered level ground, the common people were in turmoil and all fled into mountains and wilds, beyond control.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing that Deng Ai had reached level ground, the common people were in turmoil and all fled into the mountains and wilds, beyond anyone's control.

sentences.zh: 漢主使群臣會議，或以為蜀之與吳，本為與國，宜可奔吳；

translations.literal: The Lord of Han had the ministers meet in council; some thought that Shu and Wu were originally allied states and that flight to Wu would be suitable;
translations.idiomatic: The Shu ruler summoned the ministers to council. Some argued that Shu and Wu were allied states and that flight to Wu would be suitable.

sentences.zh: 或以為南中七郡，阻險斗絕，易以自守，宜可奔南。

translations.literal: Some thought that the seven commanderies of the south, perilous and isolated, were easy to hold and that flight south would be suitable.
translations.idiomatic: Others argued that the seven commanderies of the south, perilous and isolated, would be easy to hold and that flight south would be suitable.

sentences.zh: 光祿大夫譙周以為：「自古以來，無寄他國為天子者，今若入吳國，亦當臣服。

translations.literal: Director of Imperial Banquets Qiao Zhou held that, "From antiquity there has never been one who lodged in another state as Son of Heaven; if we now enter Wu, we too must submit as subjects.
translations.idiomatic: Director of Imperial Banquets Qiao Zhou argued, "From antiquity there has never been a Son of Heaven who took refuge in another state. If we now flee to Wu, we too must submit as subjects.

sentences.zh: 且治政不殊，則大能吞小，此數之自然也。

translations.literal: Moreover, when governance is not different, the large can swallow the small—this is the natural order of numbers.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, when governance is not fundamentally different, the large state can swallow the small—this is the natural order of things.

sentences.zh: 由此言之，則魏能並吳，吳不能並魏明矣。

translations.literal: From this it follows that Wei can annex Wu, but Wu cannot annex Wei—this is clear.
translations.idiomatic: From this it follows that Wei can annex Wu, but Wu cannot annex Wei—this much is clear.

sentences.zh: 等為稱臣，為小孰與為大！

translations.literal: If both mean submitting as subjects, which is better—to be small or to be large!
translations.idiomatic: If both options mean submitting as subjects, which is better—to be subject to the smaller power or to the larger!

sentences.zh: 再辱之恥何與一辱！

translations.literal: What comparison is there between the shame of two humiliations and one humiliation!
translations.idiomatic: What comparison is there between the shame of two humiliations and the shame of one!

sentences.zh: 且若欲奔南，則當早為之計，然後可果。

translations.literal: Moreover, if one wishes to flee south, one should plan for it early, and only then can it succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, if we wish to flee south, we should have planned for it early—only then could it succeed.

sentences.zh: 今大敵已近，禍敗將及，群小之心，無一可保，恐發足之日，其變不測，何至南之有乎！」

translations.literal: Now the great enemy is near, disaster and defeat are imminent, and the hearts of the petty cannot be trusted at all—I fear that on the day we set out, unforeseen changes will occur—how could we ever reach the south!"
translations.idiomatic: Now the great enemy is near, disaster and defeat are imminent, and the hearts of the petty cannot be trusted at all. I fear that on the day we set out, unforeseen changes will occur—how could we ever reach the south!"

sentences.zh: 或曰：「今艾已不遠，恐不受降，如之何？」

translations.literal: Someone said, "Ai is already not far away—I fear he will not accept surrender; what then?"
translations.idiomatic: Someone asked, "Deng Ai is already close at hand—I fear he will not accept surrender. What then?"

sentences.zh: 周曰：「方今東吳未賓，事勢不得不受，受之不得不禮。

translations.literal: Zhou said, "At present Eastern Wu has not submitted; given the situation he cannot but accept, and having accepted he cannot but treat us with courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: Qiao Zhou replied, "At present Eastern Wu has not submitted. Given the situation Deng Ai cannot but accept surrender, and having accepted he cannot but treat us with courtesy.

sentences.zh: 若陛下降魏，魏不裂土以封陛下者，周請身詣京都，以古義爭之。」

translations.literal: If Your Majesty submits to Wei and Wei does not enfeoff Your Majesty with territory, Zhou requests to go in person to the capital and argue by ancient principle."
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty submits to Wei and Wei does not enfeoff you with territory, I myself will go to the capital and argue the matter by ancient principle."

sentences.zh: 眾人皆從周議。

translations.literal: The assembly all followed Zhou's proposal.
translations.idiomatic: The assembly all followed Qiao Zhou's proposal.

sentences.zh: 漢主猶欲入南，狐疑未決。

translations.literal: The Lord of Han still wished to go south, hesitating and undecided.
translations.idiomatic: The Shu ruler still wished to flee south, hesitating and undecided.

sentences.zh: 周上疏曰：「南方遠夷之地，平常無所供為，猶數反叛，自丞相亮以兵威逼之，窮乃率從。

translations.literal: Zhou submitted a memorial, saying, "The south is distant barbarian territory; ordinarily it provides nothing, and even so it has repeatedly rebelled; only since Chancellor Liang compelled it by military might have the desperate finally submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Qiao Zhou submitted a memorial, saying, "The south is distant barbarian territory that ordinarily provides nothing, and even so it has repeatedly rebelled. Only since Chancellor Zhuge Liang compelled it by military might have the desperate finally submitted.

sentences.zh: 今若至南，外當拒敵，內供服御，費用張廣，他無所取，耗損諸夷，其叛必矣！」

translations.literal: If we now go south, we must resist the enemy without while supplying the court within; expenses will swell greatly with no other source of revenue—exhausting the various tribes, they will surely rebel!"
translations.idiomatic: If we now flee south, we must resist the enemy without while supplying the court within. Expenses will swell greatly with no other source of revenue—exhausting the various tribes, they will surely rebel!"

sentences.zh: 漢主乃遣侍中張紹等奉璽綬以降於艾。

translations.literal: The Lord of Han then dispatched Attendant-in-Ordinary Zhang Shao and others to present the seal and cord in surrender to Ai.
translations.idiomatic: The Shu ruler then dispatched Attendant-in-Ordinary Zhang Shao and others to present the imperial seal and cord in surrender to Deng Ai.

sentences.zh: 北地王諶怒曰：「若理窮力屈，禍敗將及，便當父子君臣背城一戰，同死社稷，以見先帝可也，奈何降乎！」

translations.literal: The Prince of Beidi Chen angrily said, "If reason is exhausted and strength spent, and disaster and defeat are near, then father and son, lord and ministers should fight one battle with our backs to the city and die together for the altars of soil and grain—that would be fit to show the Former Emperor—how can we surrender!"
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Beidi, Liu Chen, angrily said, "If reason is exhausted and strength spent, and disaster is near, then father and son, lord and ministers should fight one last battle with our backs to the city wall and die together for the realm—that would be fit to show the Former Emperor. How can we surrender!"

sentences.zh: 漢主不聽。

translations.literal: The Lord of Han would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: The Shu ruler would not listen.

sentences.zh: 是日，諶哭於昭烈之廟，先殺妻子，而後自殺。

translations.literal: That day Chen wept at the temple of Zhaolie, first killed his wife and children, and then killed himself.
translations.idiomatic: That day Liu Chen wept at the temple of Emperor Zhaolie, first killed his wife and children, and then killed himself.

sentences.zh: 張紹等見鄧艾於雒，艾大喜，報書褒納。

translations.literal: Zhang Shao and the others met Deng Ai at Luo; Ai was greatly pleased and replied with a letter praising and accepting them.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shao and the others met Deng Ai at Luo. Ai was greatly pleased and replied with a letter praising and accepting the surrender.

sentences.zh: 漢主遣太僕蔣顯別敕姜維使降鐘會，又遣尚書郎李虎送士民簿於艾，戶二十八萬，口九十四萬，甲士十萬二千，吏四萬人。

translations.literal: The Lord of Han dispatched Grand Master of the Household Jiang Xian with separate orders for Jiang Wei to surrender to Zhong Hui, and also dispatched Attendant Gentleman Li Hu to send the register of people to Ai: two hundred eighty thousand households, nine hundred forty thousand persons, one hundred two thousand armored soldiers, and forty thousand officials.
translations.idiomatic: The Shu ruler dispatched Grand Master of the Household Jiang Xian with separate orders for Jiang Wei to surrender to Zhong Hui, and also dispatched Attendant Gentleman Li Hu to send the register of people to Deng Ai: two hundred eighty thousand households, nine hundred forty thousand persons, one hundred two thousand armored soldiers, and forty thousand officials.

sentences.zh: 艾至成都城北，漢主率太子諸王及群臣六十餘人，面縛輿櫬詣軍門。

translations.literal: When Ai reached the north of Chengdu, the Lord of Han led the crown prince, the princes, and more than sixty ministers, bound themselves and carried coffins to the army gate.
translations.idiomatic: When Deng Ai reached the north of Chengdu, the Shu ruler led the crown prince, the princes, and more than sixty ministers, bound themselves with cords and carried coffins to the army gate.

sentences.zh: 艾持節解縛焚櫬，延請相見；

translations.literal: Ai, holding his credentials, released their bonds and burned the coffins, and invited them to meet;
translations.idiomatic: Deng Ai, holding his imperial credentials, released their bonds and burned the coffins, and invited them to meet.

sentences.zh: 檢御將士，無得虜略，綏納降附，使復舊業；

translations.literal: he inspected and controlled the officers and soldiers, forbidding looting, pacified and received the surrendered, and let them resume their former occupations;
translations.idiomatic: He inspected and controlled the officers and soldiers, forbidding looting, pacified the surrendered, and let them resume their former occupations.

sentences.zh: 輒依鄧禹故事，承製拜漢主禪行驃騎將軍，太子奉車、諸王駙馬都尉，漢群司各隨高下拜為王官，或領艾官屬；

translations.literal: Following the precedent of Deng Yu, he received imperial commission to appoint the Lord of Han Shan as General of Rapid Cavalry, the crown prince as Bearer of the Imperial Chariot, the princes as Commandants of Escort Cavalry, and the various Shu officials according to rank as royal officers or to serve under Ai's staff;
translations.idiomatic: Following the precedent of Deng Yu, he received imperial commission to appoint Liu Shan General of Rapid Cavalry, the crown prince Bearer of the Imperial Chariot, the princes Commandants of Escort Cavalry, and the various Shu officials according to rank as royal officers or to serve under Deng Ai's staff.

sentences.zh: 以師纂領益州刺史，隴西太守牽弘等領蜀中諸郡。

translations.literal: He made Shi Zuan Inspector of Yi Province, and Longxi Governor Qian Hong and others administrators of the various Shu commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: He made Shi Zuan Inspector of Yi Province, and Longxi Governor Qian Hong and others administrators of the various Shu commanderies.

sentences.zh: 艾聞黃皓奸險，收閉，將殺之，皓賂艾左右，卒以得免。

translations.literal: Ai heard that Huang Hao was treacherous and dangerous; he arrested and imprisoned him and was about to kill him, but Hao bribed Ai's attendants and ultimately escaped death.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Ai heard that Huang Hao was treacherous and dangerous. He arrested and imprisoned him and was about to execute him, but Huang Hao bribed Ai's attendants and ultimately escaped death.

sentences.zh: 姜維等聞諸葛瞻敗，未知漢主所向，乃引軍東入於巴。

translations.literal: Jiang Wei and the others heard that Zhuge Zhan had been defeated and did not know where the Lord of Han had gone; they therefore led their army east into Ba.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Wei and the others heard that Zhuge Zhan had been defeated and did not know where the Shu ruler had gone. They therefore led their army east into Ba.

sentences.zh: 鐘會進軍至涪，遣胡烈等追維。

translations.literal: Zhong Hui advanced to Fu and dispatched Hu Lie and others to pursue Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Hui advanced to Fu and dispatched Hu Lie and others to pursue Jiang Wei.

sentences.zh: 維至郪，得漢主敕命，乃令兵悉放仗，送節傳於胡烈，自從東道與廖化、張翼、董厥等同詣會降。

translations.literal: Wei reached Qi, received the Lord of Han's command, then ordered the troops to lay down all weapons, sent the seal and credentials to Hu Lie, and himself took the eastern route with Liao Hua, Zhang Yi, Dong Jue, and others to go together to Hui and surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Wei reached Qi, received the Shu ruler's command, ordered the troops to lay down all weapons, sent the seal and credentials to Hu Lie, and himself took the eastern route with Liao Hua, Zhang Yi, Dong Jue, and others to go to Zhong Hui and surrender.

sentences.zh: 將士咸怒，拔刀斫石。

translations.literal: Officers and soldiers were all enraged and drew swords to hack at stones.
translations.idiomatic: Officers and soldiers were all enraged and drew their swords to hack at stones.

sentences.zh: 於是諸郡縣圍守皆被漢主敕罷兵降。

translations.literal: Thereupon the various commanderies and districts under siege all received the Lord of Han's command to cease arms and surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the various commanderies and districts under siege all received the Shu ruler's command to cease arms and surrender.

sentences.zh: 鍾會厚待姜維等，皆權還其印綬節蓋。

translations.literal: Zhong Hui treated Jiang Wei and the others generously and temporarily returned their seals, cords, credentials, and parasols.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Hui treated Jiang Wei and the others generously and temporarily returned their seals, cords, credentials, and parasols.

sentences.zh: 吳人聞蜀已亡，乃罷丁奉等兵。

translations.literal: When the people of Wu heard that Shu had perished, they then dismissed the troops of Ding Feng and the others.
translations.idiomatic: When the people of Wu heard that Shu had fallen, they dismissed the troops of Ding Feng and the others.

sentences.zh: 吳中書丞吳郡華覈詣宮門上表曰：「伏聞成都不守，臣主播越，社稷傾覆，失委附之土，棄貢獻之國，臣以草芥，竊懷不寧。

translations.literal: Hua He of Wu Commandery, Assistant Director of the Secretariat, went to the palace gate and submitted a memorial, saying, "I have heard that Chengdu is lost; my lord drifts in peril, the altars of soil and grain are overturned, we have lost subject territory and abandoned a tributary state—as a blade of grass I privately feel uneasy.
translations.idiomatic: Hua He of Wu Commandery, Assistant Director of the Secretariat, went to the palace gate and submitted a memorial, saying, "I have heard that Chengdu is lost. My lord drifts in peril, the realm is overturned, we have lost subject territory and abandoned a tributary state. As a blade of grass I cannot rest easy.

sentences.zh: 陛下聖仁，恩澤遠撫，卒聞如此，必垂哀悼。

translations.literal: Your Majesty is sage and benevolent, your grace extends far in comfort; suddenly hearing such news, you will surely show mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty is sage and benevolent, your grace extends far in comfort. On suddenly hearing such news, you will surely show mourning.

sentences.zh: 臣不勝忡悵之情，謹拜表以聞！」

translations.literal: Your subject cannot overcome feelings of sorrow and distress; I respectfully submit this memorial to inform you!"
translations.idiomatic: Your subject cannot overcome feelings of sorrow and distress. I respectfully submit this memorial to inform you!"

sentences.zh: 魏之伐蜀也，吳人或謂襄陽張悌曰：「司馬氏得政以來，大難屢作，百姓未服，今又勞力遠征，敗於不暇，何以能克！」

translations.literal: When Wei attacked Shu, some in Wu said to Zhang Ti of Xiangyang, "Since the Sima clan took power, great calamities have repeatedly occurred, the people are not yet submissive, and now they again exhaust strength on a distant campaign—they will fail before they can finish—how can they succeed!"
translations.idiomatic: When Wei attacked Shu, some in Wu said to Zhang Ti of Xiangyang, "Since the Sima clan took power, great calamities have repeatedly occurred and the people are not yet submissive. Now they again exhaust their strength on a distant campaign—they will fail before they can finish. How can they succeed!"

sentences.zh: 悌曰：「不然。

translations.literal: Ti said, "Not so.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Ti replied, "Not so.

sentences.zh: 曹操雖功蓋中夏，民畏其威而不懷其德也。

translations.literal: Although Cao Cao's achievements covered the Central Realm, the people feared his might but did not cherish his virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Although Cao Cao's achievements covered the Central Realm, the people feared his might but did not cherish his virtue.

sentences.zh: 丕、睿承之，刑繁役重，東西驅馳，無有寧歲。

translations.literal: Pi and Rui succeeded him; punishments were many and corvée heavy, driving east and west, with no year of peace.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Pi and Cao Rui succeeded him. Punishments were many and corvée heavy, driving the people east and west, with no year of peace.

sentences.zh: 司馬懿父子累有大功，除其煩苛而布其平惠，為之謀主而救其疾苦，民心歸之亦已久矣。

translations.literal: Sima Yi and his sons repeatedly achieved great merit, removed their burdensome harshness and spread their even kindness, served as strategists for them and relieved their hardships—the people's hearts have turned to them for a long time.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yi and his sons repeatedly achieved great merit, removed burdensome harshness and spread even kindness, served as their strategists and relieved their hardships. The people's hearts have turned to them for a long time.

sentences.zh: 故淮南三叛，而腹心不擾；

translations.literal: Therefore the three rebellions in Huainan did not disturb the heartland;
translations.idiomatic: Therefore the three rebellions in Huainan did not disturb the heartland.

sentences.zh: 曹髦之死，四方不動。

translations.literal: At Cao Mao's death, the four quarters did not stir.
translations.idiomatic: At Cao Mao's death, the four quarters did not stir.

sentences.zh: 任賢使能，各盡其心，其本根固矣，奸計立矣。

translations.literal: They employ the worthy and use the capable, each giving their full heart—their roots are firm and their stratagems established.
translations.idiomatic: They employ the worthy and use the capable, each giving their full heart. Their roots are firm and their stratagems established.

sentences.zh: 今蜀閹宦專朝，國無政令，而玩戎黷武，民勞卒敝，競於外利，不修守備。

translations.literal: Now in Shu eunuchs monopolize the court, the state has no governmental orders, yet they toy with arms and abuse warfare; the people and soldiers are exhausted, competing for external gain without repairing defenses.
translations.idiomatic: Now in Shu eunuchs monopolize the court, the state has no governmental orders, yet they toy with arms and abuse warfare. The people and soldiers are exhausted, competing for external gain without repairing defenses.

sentences.zh: 彼強弱不同，智算亦勝，因危而伐，殆無不克。

translations.literal: Their strength and weakness differ, their wisdom and calculation also prevail—striking while they are in peril, there is scarcely anything they cannot overcome.
translations.idiomatic: Their strength and weakness differ, and their wisdom and calculation also prevail. Striking while Shu is in peril, there is scarcely anything they cannot overcome.

sentences.zh: 噫！

translations.literal: Alas!
translations.idiomatic: Alas!

sentences.zh: 彼之得志，我之憂也。」

translations.literal: Their success is our worry."
translations.idiomatic: Their success is our worry."

sentences.zh: 吳人笑其言，至是乃服。

translations.literal: The people of Wu laughed at his words; only at this point did they submit to them.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Wu laughed at his words. Only now did they submit to them.

sentences.zh: 吳人以武陵五溪夷與蜀接界，蜀亡，懼其叛亂，乃以越騎校尉鐘離牧領武陵太守。

translations.literal: The people of Wu, because the Wuling Five Streams Yi bordered Shu, feared rebellion after Shu's fall and therefore made Commandant of Flying Cavalry Zhongli Mu lead as Governor of Wuling.
translations.idiomatic: Because the Wuling Five Streams Yi bordered Shu, the Wu court feared rebellion after Shu's fall and made Commandant of Flying Cavalry Zhongli Mu Governor of Wuling.

sentences.zh: 魏已遣漢葭縣長郭純試守武陵太守，率涪陵民入遷陵界，屯於赤沙，誘動諸夷進攻酉陽，郡中震懼。

translations.literal: Wei had already dispatched Guo Chun, magistrate of Jia County in Han, to trial-govern Wuling; he led people of Fuling into Qianling territory, encamped at Chisha, and incited the various Yi to attack Youyang—the commandery was shaken with fear.
translations.idiomatic: Wei had already dispatched Guo Chun, magistrate of Jia County in Han, to trial-govern Wuling. He led people of Fuling into Qianling territory, encamped at Chisha, and incited the various Yi to attack Youyang. The commandery was shaken with fear.

sentences.zh: 牧問朝吏曰：「西蜀傾覆，邊境見侵，何以御之？」

translations.literal: Mu asked the court officials, saying, "Western Shu has fallen, the border is being invaded—how shall we resist it?"
translations.idiomatic: Zhongli Mu asked the court officials, "Western Shu has fallen and the border is being invaded. How shall we resist it?"

sentences.zh: 皆對曰：「今二縣山險，諸夷阻兵，不可以軍驚擾，驚擾則諸夷盤結；

translations.literal: All replied, "Now the two counties are mountainous and perilous, the various Yi hold arms—troops must not be used to alarm them; if alarmed the Yi will band together;
translations.idiomatic: All replied, "The two counties are mountainous and perilous, and the various Yi hold arms. Troops must not be used to alarm them, for if alarmed the Yi will band together.

sentences.zh: 宜以漸安，可遣恩信吏宣教慰勞。」

translations.literal: It is suitable to pacify them gradually; trustworthy officials may be sent to instruct, comfort, and reassure them."
translations.idiomatic: It is better to pacify them gradually by sending trustworthy officials to instruct, comfort, and reassure them."

sentences.zh: 牧曰：「不然。

translations.literal: Mu said, "Not so.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongli Mu said, "Not so.

sentences.zh: 外境內侵，誑誘人民，當及其根柢未深而撲取之，此救火貴速之勢也。」

translations.literal: Foreign territory invades within and deceives the people—we should strike while their roots are not yet deep, like the urgency of fighting fire."
translations.idiomatic: Foreign territory invades within and deceives the people. We should strike while their roots are not yet deep—this is like the urgency of fighting fire."

sentences.zh: 敕外趣嚴。

translations.literal: He ordered preparations to be hastened.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered preparations to be hastened.

sentences.zh: 撫夷將軍高尚謂牧曰：「昔淵太常督兵五萬，然後討五溪夷。

translations.literal: General Who Pacifies the Yi Gao Shang said to Mu, "Formerly Director of Ceremonies Yuan led fifty thousand troops before subduing the Five Streams Yi.
translations.idiomatic: General Who Pacifies the Yi Gao Shang said to Zhongli Mu, "Formerly Director of Ceremonies Sun Yuan led fifty thousand troops before subduing the Five Streams Yi.

sentences.zh: 是時劉氏連和，諸夷率化。

translations.literal: At that time the Liu clan was allied with them, and the various Yi mostly submitted.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Liu clan was allied with them, and the various Yi mostly submitted.

sentences.zh: 今既無往日之援，而郭純已據遷陵，而明府欲以三千兵深入，尚未見其利也。」

translations.literal: Now there is no aid as in former days, and Guo Chun already holds Qianling—yet Your Excellency wishes to penetrate deeply with three thousand troops; the advantage is not yet seen."
translations.idiomatic: Now there is no aid as in former days, and Guo Chun already holds Qianling. Yet Your Excellency wishes to penetrate deeply with only three thousand troops—the advantage is not yet clear."

sentences.zh: 牧曰：「非常之事，何得循舊！」

translations.literal: Mu said, "Extraordinary matters—how can one follow old ways!"
translations.idiomatic: Zhongli Mu said, "These are extraordinary matters—how can one follow old ways!"

sentences.zh: 即率所領晨夜進道，緣山險行垂二千里，斬惡民懷異心者魁帥百餘人，及其支黨凡千餘級。

translations.literal: He immediately led his command day and night on the march, traveling nearly two thousand li along perilous mountains, beheading more than a hundred chieftains among wicked people with disloyal hearts and more than a thousand of their followers in all.
