translations.idiomatic: He immediately led his command day and night on the march, traveling nearly two thousand li along perilous mountains. He beheaded more than a hundred chieftains among wicked people with disloyal hearts and more than a thousand of their followers in all.

sentences.zh: 純等散走，五溪皆平。

translations.literal: Chun and the others scattered and fled; the Five Streams were all pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Chun and the others scattered and fled. The Five Streams were all pacified.

sentences.zh: 十二月，庚戌，以司徒鄭沖為太保。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on day gengxu, Minister over the Masses Zheng Chong was made Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on the day gengxu, Minister over the Masses Zheng Chong was made Grand Tutor.

sentences.zh: 壬子，分益州為梁州。

translations.literal: On day renzi, Yi Province was divided to form Liang Province.
translations.idiomatic: On the day renzi, Yi Province was divided to form Liang Province.

sentences.zh: 癸丑，特赦益州士民，復除租稅之半五年。

translations.literal: On day guichou, a special amnesty was granted to the gentry and people of Yi Province, and half their rent and taxes were remitted for five years.
translations.idiomatic: On the day guichou, a special amnesty was granted to the gentry and people of Yi Province, and half their rent and taxes were remitted for five years.

sentences.zh: 乙卯，以鄧艾為太尉，增邑二萬戶；

translations.literal: On day yimao, Deng Ai was made Grand Commandant and his fief increased by twenty thousand households;
translations.idiomatic: On the day yimao, Deng Ai was made Grand Commandant and his fief was increased by twenty thousand households.

sentences.zh: 鍾會為司徒，增邑萬戶。

translations.literal: Zhong Hui was made Minister over the Masses and his fief increased by ten thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Hui was made Minister over the Masses and his fief was increased by ten thousand households.

sentences.zh: 皇太后郭氏殂。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Lady Guo died.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Lady Guo died.

sentences.zh: 鄧艾在成都，頗自矜伐，謂蜀士大夫曰：「諸君賴遭艾，故得有今日耳。

translations.literal: Deng Ai was in Chengdu and rather praised himself, saying to the Shu gentry and officials, "You gentlemen rely on encountering Ai to have today.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Ai was in Chengdu and rather praised himself, saying to the Shu gentry and officials, "You gentlemen owe your survival today to encountering me.

sentences.zh: 如遇吳漢之徒，已殄滅矣。」

translations.literal: If you had met men like Wu Han, you would already have been exterminated."
translations.idiomatic: If you had met men like Wu Han, you would already have been exterminated."

sentences.zh: 艾以書言於晉公昭曰：「兵有先聲而後實者，今因平蜀之勢以乘吳，吳人震恐，席捲之時也。

translations.literal: Ai wrote to Duke of Jin Zhao, saying, "In warfare there is first reputation and then substance; now riding the momentum of pacifying Shu to strike Wu, the Wu people are shaken with fear—this is the time to sweep them up.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Ai wrote to Duke of Jin Sima Zhao, saying, "In warfare there is first reputation and then substance. Now, riding the momentum of pacifying Shu to strike Wu, the Wu people are shaken with fear—this is the time to sweep them up.

sentences.zh: 然大舉之後，將士疲勞，不可使用，且徐緩之。

translations.literal: Yet after a great campaign the officers and soldiers are weary and cannot be used; it should be slowed for the moment.
translations.idiomatic: Yet after a great campaign the officers and soldiers are weary and cannot be used. For the moment it should be slowed.

sentences.zh: 留隴右兵二萬人、蜀兵二萬人，煮鹽興冶，為軍農要用，並作舟船，豫為順流之事。

translations.literal: Leave twenty thousand Longyou troops and twenty thousand Shu troops, boil salt and develop smelting as essential military agriculture, and also build boats in preparation for downstream operations.
translations.idiomatic: Leave twenty thousand Longyou troops and twenty thousand Shu troops, boil salt and develop smelting as essential military agriculture, and also build boats in preparation for downstream operations.

sentences.zh: 然後發使告以利害，吳必歸化，可不征而定也。

translations.literal: Then send envoys to explain advantage and harm—Wu will surely submit, and can be settled without campaigning.
translations.idiomatic: Then send envoys to explain advantage and harm. Wu will surely submit and can be settled without campaigning.

sentences.zh: 今宜厚劉禪以致孫休，封禪為扶風王，錫其資財，供其左右，郡有董卓塢，為之宮捨，爵其子為公侯，食郡內縣，以顯歸命之寵；

translations.literal: Now Liu Shan should be treated generously to influence Sun Xiu; Shan should be enfeoffed as King of Fufeng, granted assets, and supplied for his attendants; in the commandery is Dong Zhuo's fort—make it his palace residence; ennoble his sons as marquises and dukes with counties within the commandery as their fiefs, to display the favor of submission;
translations.idiomatic: Now Liu Shan should be treated generously to influence Sun Xiu. Shan should be enfeoffed as King of Fufeng, granted assets, and supplied for his attendants. In the commandery is Dong Zhuo's fort—make it his palace residence. Ennoble his sons as marquises and dukes with counties within the commandery as their fiefs, to display the favor granted to those who submit.

sentences.zh: 開廣陵、城陽以待吳人，則畏威懷德，望風而從矣！」

translations.literal: Open Guangling and Chengyang to await the Wu people, and they will fear the might and cherish the virtue, following at the first wind!"
translations.idiomatic: Open Guangling and Chengyang to await the Wu people, and they will fear the might and cherish the virtue, following at the first wind!"

sentences.zh: 昭使監軍衛瓘諭艾：「事當須報，不宜輒行。」

translations.literal: Zhao sent Army Supervisor Wei Guan to instruct Ai, saying, "Matters must be reported; they should not be carried out on one's own authority."
translations.idiomatic: Sima Zhao sent Army Supervisor Wei Guan to instruct Deng Ai, saying, "Matters must be reported. They should not be carried out on one's own authority."

sentences.zh: 艾重言曰：「銜命征行，奉指授之策，元惡既服，至於承製拜假，以安初附，謂合權宜。

translations.literal: Ai spoke again, saying, "Bearing orders on campaign and following the strategy entrusted to me, once the chief villain submitted, as for receiving imperial commission to grant appointments in order to pacify the newly submitted, I considered this suitable expedience.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Ai spoke again, saying, "Bearing orders on campaign and following the strategy entrusted to me, once the chief villain submitted, receiving imperial commission to grant appointments in order to pacify the newly submitted—I considered this suitable expedience.

sentences.zh: 今蜀舉眾歸命，地盡南海，東接吳、會，宜早鎮定。

translations.literal: Now Shu has submitted with all its people; the land extends to the Southern Sea and east connects with Wu and Kuaiji—it should be pacified early.
translations.idiomatic: Now Shu has submitted with all its people. The land extends to the Southern Sea and east connects with Wu and Kuaiji—it should be pacified early.

sentences.zh: 若待國命，往復道途，延引日月。

translations.literal: If one waits for national orders, going back and forth on the roads, days and months will be drawn out.
translations.idiomatic: If one waits for national orders, going back and forth on the roads, days and months will be drawn out.

sentences.zh: 《春秋》之義，『大夫出疆，有可以安社稷、利國家，專之可也。』

translations.literal: The meaning of the Spring and Autumn Annals is: 'When a grandee goes beyond the border, if there is something that can secure the altars of soil and grain and benefit the state, he may decide it on his own authority.'
translations.idiomatic: The meaning of the Spring and Autumn Annals is: 'When a grandee goes beyond the border, if there is something that can secure the altars of soil and grain and benefit the state, he may decide it on his own authority.'

sentences.zh: 今吳未賓，勢與蜀連，不可拘常，以失事機。

translations.literal: Now Wu has not submitted; its situation connects with Shu—one cannot be bound by convention and lose the opportunity.
translations.idiomatic: Now Wu has not submitted and its situation connects with Shu. One cannot be bound by convention and lose the opportunity.

sentences.zh: 《兵法》：『進不求名，退不避罪。』

translations.literal: The Art of War says: 'Advance not seeking fame, retreat not avoiding blame.'
translations.idiomatic: The Art of War says: 'Advance not seeking fame, retreat not avoiding blame.'

sentences.zh: 艾雖無古人之節，終不自嫌以損國家計也！」

translations.literal: Although Ai lacks the integrity of the ancients, in the end he will not shrink from acting to the detriment of the state's plans!"
translations.idiomatic: Although I lack the integrity of the ancients, in the end I will not shrink from acting to the detriment of the state's plans!"

sentences.zh: 鐘會內有異志，姜維知之，欲構成擾亂，乃說會曰：「聞君自淮南已來，算無遺策，晉道克昌，皆君之力。

translations.literal: Zhong Hui harbored rebellious intent within; Jiang Wei knew this and wished to create disturbance; he therefore said to Hui, "I hear that since Huainan you have had no plan left unfulfilled; the Jin way has flourished—all is your power.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Hui harbored rebellious intent within. Jiang Wei knew this and wished to create disturbance. He therefore said to Hui, "I hear that since Huainan you have had no plan left unfulfilled. The Jin way has flourished—all through your power.

sentences.zh: 今復定蜀，威德振世，民高其功，主畏其謀，欲以此安歸乎！

translations.literal: Now you have again pacified Shu; your prestige and virtue shake the age; the people exalt your achievement and the ruler fears your stratagems—do you wish to settle safely on this basis!
translations.idiomatic: Now you have again pacified Shu. Your prestige and virtue shake the age. The people exalt your achievement and the ruler fears your stratagems. Do you think you can settle safely on this basis!

sentences.zh: 何不法陶朱公泛舟絕跡，全功保身邪！」

translations.literal: Why not follow Lord Tao Zhu, drifting on the waters and vanishing without trace, preserving your achievement and keeping yourself safe!"
translations.idiomatic: Why not follow Lord Tao Zhu, drifting on the waters and vanishing without trace, preserving your achievement and keeping yourself safe!"

sentences.zh: 會曰：「君言遠矣，我不能行。

translations.literal: Hui said, "Your words are far-reaching; I cannot act on them.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Hui said, "Your words are far-reaching. I cannot act on them.

sentences.zh: 且為今之道，或未盡於此也。」

translations.literal: Moreover, as for the way of today, it may not be exhausted in this alone."
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, as for the way forward today, it may not be exhausted in this alone."

sentences.zh: 維曰：「其他則君智力之所能，無煩於老夫矣。」

translations.literal: Wei said, "As for the rest, that is within your wisdom and power—I need not trouble this old man."
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Wei said, "As for the rest, that is within your wisdom and power. I need not trouble myself with it."

sentences.zh: 由是情好歡甚，出則同輿，坐則同席，會因鄧艾承製專事，乃與衛瓘密白艾有反狀。

translations.literal: From this their friendship was very warm; going out they shared a carriage, sitting they shared a mat. Because Deng Ai received imperial commission and acted on his own authority, Hui secretly reported to Wei Guan that Ai showed signs of rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: From this their friendship grew very warm. Going out they shared a carriage; sitting they shared a mat. Because Deng Ai received imperial commission and acted on his own authority, Zhong Hui secretly reported to Wei Guan that Ai showed signs of rebellion.

sentences.zh: 會善效人書，於劍閣要艾章表、白事，皆易其言，令辭指悖傲，多自矜伐；

translations.literal: Hui was skilled at imitating others' handwriting; at Jian'ge he intercepted Ai's memorials and reports, all altering their wording to make the tone arrogant and self-praising;
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Hui was skilled at imitating others' handwriting. At Jian'ge he intercepted Ai's memorials and reports and altered their wording to make the tone arrogant and self-praising.

sentences.zh: 又毀晉公昭報書，手作以疑之。

translations.literal: He also destroyed Duke of Jin Zhao's reply letters and wrote them himself by hand to create suspicion.
translations.idiomatic: He also destroyed Duke of Jin Sima Zhao's reply letters and wrote them himself by hand to create suspicion.

sentences.zh: 元皇帝下咸熙元年（

translations.literal: Under Emperor Yuan, first year of Xixi (
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Yuan, first year of Xixi (

sentences.zh: 甲申，公元二六四年）

translations.literal: jiashen, AD 264)
translations.idiomatic: the year jiashen, AD 264)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，壬辰，詔以檻車征鄧艾。

translations.literal: In spring, first month, on day renchen, an edict ordered Deng Ai summoned in a caged cart.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, in the first month, on the day renchen, an edict ordered Deng Ai summoned in a caged cart.

sentences.zh: 晉公昭恐艾不從命，敕鐘會進軍成都，又遣賈充將兵入斜谷。

translations.literal: Duke of Jin Zhao, fearing Ai would not obey orders, commanded Zhong Hui to advance on Chengdu and also dispatched Jia Chong to lead troops into Xiegu.
translations.idiomatic: Duke of Jin Sima Zhao, fearing Deng Ai would not obey orders, commanded Zhong Hui to advance on Chengdu and also dispatched Jia Chong to lead troops into Xiegu.

sentences.zh: 昭自將大軍從帝幸長安，以諸王公皆在鄴，乃以山濤為行軍司馬，鎮鄴。

translations.literal: Zhao himself led a great army, accompanying the emperor to Chang'an; because the various princes and dukes were all at Ye, he made Shan Tao Army Supervisor on Campaign to guard Ye.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Zhao himself led a great army, accompanying the emperor to Chang'an. Because the various princes and dukes were all at Ye, he made Shan Tao Army Supervisor on Campaign to guard Ye.

sentences.zh: 初，鐘會以才能見任，昭夫人王氏言於昭曰：「會見利忘義，好為事端，寵過必亂，不可大任。」

translations.literal: At the outset, because Zhong Hui's talent was recognized and he was entrusted with office, Zhao's wife Lady Wang said to Zhao, "Hui sees profit and forgets righteousness, loves to create incidents—excessive favor will surely bring disorder; he cannot be greatly entrusted."
translations.idiomatic: At the outset, because Zhong Hui's talent was recognized and he was entrusted with office, Zhao's wife Lady Wang said to Zhao, "Hui sees profit and forgets righteousness and loves to create incidents. Excessive favor will surely bring disorder. He cannot be greatly entrusted."

sentences.zh: 及會將伐漢，西曹屬邵悌言於晉公曰：「今遣鐘會率十萬餘眾伐蜀，愚謂令單身無任，不若使餘人行也。」

translations.literal: When Hui was about to attack Han, Western Bureau Aide Shao Ti said to the Duke of Jin, "Now dispatching Zhong Hui to lead more than one hundred thousand troops to attack Shu, I foolishly think that giving him sole authority without restraint is not as good as sending others as well."
translations.idiomatic: When Hui was about to attack Shu, Western Bureau Aide Shao Ti said to the Duke of Jin, "Now you are dispatching Zhong Hui to lead more than one hundred thousand troops to attack Shu. I think giving him sole authority without restraint is not as good as sending others as well."

sentences.zh: 晉公笑曰：「我寧不知此邪！

translations.literal: The Duke of Jin smiled and said, "Do you think I do not know this!
translations.idiomatic: The Duke of Jin smiled and said, "Do you think I do not know this!

sentences.zh: 蜀數為邊寇，師老民疲，我今伐之，如指掌耳，而眾方蜀不可伐。

translations.literal: Shu has repeatedly raided the borders; the armies are worn and the people exhausted—I now attack it as easily as pointing at my palm, yet everyone says Shu cannot be attacked.
translations.idiomatic: Shu has repeatedly raided the borders. The armies are worn and the people exhausted. I now attack it as easily as pointing at my palm, yet everyone says Shu cannot be attacked.

sentences.zh: 夫人心豫怯則智勇並竭，智勇並竭而強使之，適所以為敵禽耳。

translations.literal: When people's hearts are beforehand timid, wisdom and courage are both exhausted; when wisdom and courage are both exhausted and they are forced, that is precisely how to become the enemy's prey.
translations.idiomatic: When people's hearts are beforehand timid, wisdom and courage are both exhausted. When wisdom and courage are both exhausted and they are forced into action, that is precisely how to become the enemy's prey.

sentences.zh: 惟鐘會與人意同，今遣會伐蜀，蜀必可滅。

translations.literal: Only Zhong Hui agrees with my intent; now dispatching Hui to attack Shu, Shu can surely be destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Only Zhong Hui agrees with my intent. Now, dispatching him to attack Shu, Shu can surely be destroyed.

sentences.zh: 滅蜀之後，就如卿慮，何憂其不能辦邪？

translations.literal: After Shu is destroyed, even if it is as you worry, why fear that it cannot be handled?
translations.idiomatic: After Shu is destroyed, even if it is as you worry, why fear that it cannot be handled?

sentences.zh: 夫蜀已破亡，遺民震恐，不足與共圖事；

translations.literal: Shu is already broken and perished; the surviving people are shaken with fear—not enough to plot affairs together;
translations.idiomatic: Shu is already broken and perished. The surviving people are shaken with fear—not enough to plot affairs together.

sentences.zh: 中國將士各自思歸，不肯與同也。

translations.literal: The Central Realm's officers and soldiers each think of returning home and will not join with him.
translations.idiomatic: The Central Realm's officers and soldiers each think of returning home and will not join with him.

sentences.zh: 會若作惡，只自滅族耳。

translations.literal: If Hui does evil, he will only destroy his own clan.
translations.idiomatic: If Hui does evil, he will only destroy his own clan.

sentences.zh: 卿不須憂此，慎勿使人聞也！」

translations.literal: You need not worry about this—be careful not to let anyone hear!"
translations.idiomatic: You need not worry about this. Be careful not to let anyone hear!"

sentences.zh: 及晉公將之長安，悌復曰：「鐘會所統兵五六倍於鄧艾，但可敕會取艾，不須自行。」

translations.literal: When the Duke of Jin was about to go to Chang'an, Ti again said, "The troops Zhong Hui commands are five or six times those of Deng Ai—it is enough to command Hui to seize Ai; there is no need to go yourself."
translations.idiomatic: When the Duke of Jin was about to go to Chang'an, Shao Ti again said, "The troops Zhong Hui commands are five or six times those of Deng Ai. It is enough to command Hui to seize Ai. There is no need for you to go yourself."

sentences.zh: 晉公曰：「卿忘前言邪，而雲不須行乎？

translations.literal: The Duke of Jin said, "Have you forgotten your earlier words, yet say there is no need to go?
translations.idiomatic: The Duke of Jin said, "Have you forgotten your earlier words, yet say there is no need to go?

sentences.zh: 雖然，所言不可宣也。

translations.literal: Even so, what was said must not be proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: Even so, what was said must not be proclaimed.

sentences.zh: 我要自當以信意待人，但人不當負我耳，我豈可先人生心哉！

translations.literal: I myself should treat people with trust and good faith—only people should not fail me; how could I first harbor suspicion in my heart!
translations.idiomatic: I myself should treat people with trust and good faith. Only people should not fail me. How could I first harbor suspicion in my heart!

sentences.zh: 近日賈護軍問我：『頗疑鐘會不？』

translations.literal: Recently Protector of the Army Jia asked me, 'Do you rather suspect Zhong Hui?'
translations.idiomatic: Recently Protector of the Army Jia Chong asked me, 'Do you rather suspect Zhong Hui?'

sentences.zh: 還答言：『如今遣卿行，寧可復疑卿邪？』

translations.literal: I answered, 'Now that I am sending you on campaign, could I again suspect you?'
translations.idiomatic: I answered, 'Now that I am sending you on campaign, could I again suspect you?'

sentences.zh: 賈亦無以易我語也。

translations.literal: Jia also had nothing with which to change my words.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Chong also had nothing with which to change my words.

sentences.zh: 我到長安，則自了矣。」

translations.literal: When I reach Chang'an, it will settle itself."
translations.idiomatic: When I reach Chang'an, it will settle itself."

sentences.zh: 鐘會遣衛瓘先至成都收鄧艾，會以瓘兵少，欲令艾殺瓘，因以為艾罪。

translations.literal: Zhong Hui dispatched Wei Guan first to Chengdu to seize Deng Ai; Hui, because Guan's troops were few, wished to have Ai kill Guan and thereby make it Ai's crime.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Hui dispatched Wei Guan first to Chengdu to seize Deng Ai. Because Guan's troops were few, Hui wished to have Ai kill Guan and thereby make it Ai's crime.

sentences.zh: 瓘知其意，然不可得距，乃夜至成都，檄艾所統諸將，稱：「奉詔收艾，其餘一無所問；

translations.literal: Guan knew his intent but could not refuse; he therefore arrived at Chengdu by night and issued a proclamation to the generals under Ai, stating, "By imperial edict we seize Ai; as for the rest we ask nothing;
translations.idiomatic: Guan knew his intent but could not refuse. He therefore arrived at Chengdu by night and issued a proclamation to the generals under Ai, stating, "By imperial edict we seize Ai. As for the rest we ask nothing.

sentences.zh: 若來赴官軍，爵賞如先；

translations.literal: If you come to join the official army, titles and rewards are as before;
translations.idiomatic: If you come to join the official army, titles and rewards are as before.

sentences.zh: 敢有不出，誅及三族！」

translations.literal: If anyone dares not come out, punishment extends to three clans!"
translations.idiomatic: If anyone dares not come out, punishment extends to three clans!"

sentences.zh: 比至雞鳴，悉來赴瓘，唯艾帳內在焉。

translations.literal: By the time of the cock's crow all had come to join Guan; only those within Ai's tent remained.
translations.idiomatic: By the time of the cock's crow all had come to join Guan. Only those within Ai's tent remained.

sentences.zh: 平旦，開門，瓘乘使者車，逕入至艾所居；

translations.literal: At dawn the gate was opened; Guan rode the envoy's carriage and went straight in to where Ai lived;
translations.idiomatic: At dawn the gate was opened. Guan rode the envoy's carriage and went straight in to where Ai lived.

sentences.zh: 艾尚臥未起，遂執艾父子，置艾於檻車。

translations.literal: Ai was still lying down and had not risen; they then seized Ai and his son and placed Ai in a caged cart.
translations.idiomatic: Ai was still lying down and had not risen. They then seized Ai and his son and placed Ai in a caged cart.

sentences.zh: 諸將圖欲劫艾，整仗趣瓘營；

translations.literal: The generals plotted to rescue Ai, arrayed their weapons, and hastened toward Guan's camp;
translations.idiomatic: The generals plotted to rescue Ai, arrayed their weapons, and hastened toward Guan's camp.

sentences.zh: 瓘輕出迎之，偽作表草，將申明艾事，諸將信之而止。

translations.literal: Guan went out lightly to meet them, falsely drafting a memorial about to clarify Ai's case; the generals believed him and stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Guan went out lightly to meet them, falsely drafting a memorial about to clarify Ai's case. The generals believed him and stopped.

sentences.zh: 丙子，會至成都，送艾赴京師。

translations.literal: On day bingzi, Hui reached Chengdu and sent Ai to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: On the day bingzi, Zhong Hui reached Chengdu and sent Ai to the capital.

sentences.zh: 會所憚惟艾，艾父子既禽，會獨統大眾，威震西土，遂決意謀反。

translations.literal: The one Hui feared was only Ai; once Ai and his son were captured, Hui alone commanded the great host, his prestige shaking the western lands, and he therefore resolved to rebel.
translations.idiomatic: The one Hui feared was only Ai. Once Ai and his son were captured, Hui alone commanded the great host, his prestige shaking the western lands, and he therefore resolved to rebel.

sentences.zh: 會欲使姜維將五萬人出斜谷為前驅，會自將大眾隨其後，既至長安，令騎士從陸道，步兵從水道，順流浮渭入河，以為五日可到孟津，與騎兵會洛陽，一旦天下可定也。

translations.literal: Hui wished to have Jiang Wei lead fifty thousand men out through Xiegu as vanguard; Hui himself would lead the great host after them. Reaching Chang'an, he would have horsemen go by land route and foot soldiers by water route, floating down the Wei into the Yellow River, thinking that in five days they could reach Mengjin, join cavalry at Luoyang, and in one morning the realm could be settled.
translations.idiomatic: Hui wished to have Jiang Wei lead fifty thousand men out through Xiegu as vanguard while he himself led the great host after them. Reaching Chang'an, he would send horsemen by land and foot soldiers by water, floating down the Wei into the Yellow River. He thought that in five days they could reach Mengjin, join cavalry at Luoyang, and in one stroke settle the realm.

sentences.zh: 會得晉公書云：「恐鄧艾或不就征，今遣中護軍賈充將步騎萬人徑入斜谷，屯樂城，吾自將十萬屯長安，相見在近。」

translations.literal: Hui received a letter from the Duke of Jin saying, "I fear Deng Ai may not obey the summons; I now dispatch Central Protector of the Army Jia Chong to lead ten thousand foot and horse straight into Xiegu and encamp at Lecheng; I myself will lead one hundred thousand and encamp at Chang'an—we shall meet soon."
translations.idiomatic: Hui received a letter from the Duke of Jin saying, "I fear Deng Ai may not obey the summons. I now dispatch Central Protector of the Army Jia Chong to lead ten thousand foot and horse straight into Xiegu and encamp at Lecheng. I myself will lead one hundred thousand and encamp at Chang'an—we shall meet soon."

sentences.zh: 會得書驚，呼所親語之曰：「但取鄧艾，相國知我獨辦之；

translations.literal: Hui was alarmed on receiving the letter and called his intimates, saying to them, "To seize Deng Ai alone—the Chancellor knows I can handle it alone;
translations.idiomatic: Hui was alarmed on receiving the letter and called his intimates, saying, "To seize Deng Ai alone—the Chancellor knows I can handle that alone.

sentences.zh: 今來大重，必覺我異矣，便當速發。

translations.literal: Now he comes in great force—he must have sensed my difference; we should act quickly.
translations.idiomatic: Now he comes in great force—he must have sensed my intentions. We must act quickly.

sentences.zh: 事成，可得天下；

translations.literal: If the affair succeeds, we can obtain the realm;
translations.idiomatic: If the affair succeeds, we can obtain the realm.

sentences.zh: 不成，退保蜀、漢，不失作劉備也！」

translations.literal: If it fails, withdraw and hold Shu and Han—we will not fail to become another Liu Bei!"
translations.idiomatic: If it fails, withdraw and hold Shu and Han—we will not fail to become another Liu Bei!"

sentences.zh: 丁丑，會番請護軍、郡守、牙門騎督以上及蜀之故官，為太后發哀於蜀朝堂，矯太后遺詔，使會起兵廢司馬昭，皆班示坐上人，使下議訖，書版署置，更使所親信代領諸軍；

translations.literal: On day dingchou, Hui repeatedly invited Protectors of the Army, commandery governors, gate cavalry commanders and above, and former Shu officials, to mourn the Empress Dowager in the Shu court hall; he forged the Empress Dowager's final edict ordering Hui to raise troops and depose Sima Zhao, displayed it to all present, had them debate and conclude, wrote and signed the roster of appointments, and replaced command of the armies with his trusted followers;
translations.idiomatic: On the day dingchou, Hui repeatedly invited Protectors of the Army, commandery governors, gate cavalry commanders and above, and former Shu officials to mourn the Empress Dowager in the Shu court hall. He forged the Empress Dowager's final edict ordering him to raise troops and depose Sima Zhao, displayed it to all present, had them debate and conclude, wrote and signed the roster of appointments, and replaced command of the armies with his trusted followers.

sentences.zh: 所請群官，番閉著益州諸曹屋中，城門宮門皆閉，嚴兵圍守。

translations.literal: The invited officials were repeatedly shut inside the offices of Yi Province; city gates and palace gates were all closed and troops strictly encircled and guarded them.
translations.idiomatic: The invited officials were repeatedly shut inside the offices of Yi Province. City gates and palace gates were all closed and troops strictly encircled and guarded them.

sentences.zh: 衛瓘詐稱疾篤，出就外廨。

translations.literal: Wei Guan falsely claimed grave illness and went out to an outer office.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Guan falsely claimed grave illness and went out to an outer office.

sentences.zh: 會信之，無所復憚。

translations.literal: Hui believed him and no longer had any fear.
translations.idiomatic: Hui believed him and no longer had any fear.

sentences.zh: 姜維欲使會盡殺北來諸將，己因殺會，盡坑魏兵，復立漢主，密書與劉禪曰：「願陛下忍數日之辱，臣欲使社稷危而復安，日月幽而復明。」

translations.literal: Jiang Wei wished to have Hui kill all the northern generals, then himself kill Hui, bury all Wei troops, restore the Lord of Han, and secretly wrote to Liu Shan, saying, "I hope Your Majesty will endure a few days' humiliation—I wish to make the altars of soil and grain, though in peril, safe again, and the sun and moon, though dark, bright again."
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Wei wished to have Hui kill all the northern generals, then himself kill Hui, bury all Wei troops, and restore the Shu ruler. He secretly wrote to Liu Shan, saying, "I hope Your Majesty will endure a few days' humiliation. I wish to make the realm, though in peril, safe again, and the sun and moon, though dark, bright again."

sentences.zh: 會欲從維言誅諸將，猶豫未決。

translations.literal: Hui wished to follow Wei's words and execute the generals, but hesitated and could not decide.
translations.idiomatic: Hui wished to follow Wei's words and execute the generals, but hesitated and could not decide.

sentences.zh: 會帳下督丘建本屬胡烈，會愛信之。

translations.literal: Qiu Jian, supervisor under Hui's tent, had originally belonged to Hu Lie; Hui loved and trusted him.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu Jian, supervisor under Hui's tent, had originally belonged to Hu Lie. Hui loved and trusted him.

sentences.zh: 建愍烈獨坐，啟會，使聽內一親兵出取飲食，諸牙門隨例各內一人。

translations.literal: Jian, pitying Lie sitting alone, reported to Hui and had him allow one personal soldier inside to fetch food and drink; each gate commander similarly had one man admitted.
translations.idiomatic: Jian, pitying Lie sitting alone, reported to Hui and had him allow one personal soldier inside to fetch food and drink. Each gate commander similarly had one man admitted.

sentences.zh: 烈紿語親兵及疏與其子淵曰：「丘建密說消息，會已作大坑，白棓數千，欲悉呼外兵入，人賜白□陷，拜散將，以次棓殺，內坑中。」

translations.literal: Lie deceived his personal soldier and in a letter to his son Yuan said, "Qiu Jian secretly told news: Hui has already dug a great pit and several thousand white clubs; he wishes to call all outside troops in, give each a white club, dismiss the generals, and beat them to death in order, casting them into the pit."
translations.idiomatic: Lie deceived his personal soldier and in a letter to his son Hu Yuan said, "Qiu Jian secretly told us: Hui has already dug a great pit and prepared several thousand white clubs. He wishes to call all outside troops in, give each a white club, dismiss the generals, and beat them to death in order, casting them into the pit."

sentences.zh: 諸牙門親兵亦咸說此語，一夜，轉相告，皆遍。

translations.literal: The personal soldiers of the various gate commanders also all spoke these words; in one night they told one another in turn until all knew.
translations.idiomatic: The personal soldiers of the various gate commanders also all spoke these words. In one night they told one another in turn until all knew.

sentences.zh: 己卯，日中，胡淵率其父兵雷鼓出門，諸軍不期皆鼓噪而出，曾無督促之者，而爭先赴城。

translations.literal: On day jimao, at midday, Hu Yuan led his father's troops, beating drums and going out the gate; the armies unexpectedly all clamored and rushed out with drums—there was no one urging them on, yet they vied to reach the city first.
translations.idiomatic: On the day jimao, at midday, Hu Yuan led his father's troops, beating drums and going out the gate. The armies unexpectedly all clamored and rushed out with drums. There was no one urging them on, yet they vied to reach the city first.

sentences.zh: 時會方給姜維鎧仗，白外有匈匈聲，似失火者，有頃，白兵走向城。

translations.literal: At the time Hui was just issuing armor and weapons to Jiang Wei; he was told there was a rumbling outside like a fire; shortly after he was told troops were marching toward the city.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Hui was just issuing armor and weapons to Jiang Wei. He was told there was a rumbling outside like a fire. Shortly after he was told troops were marching toward the city.

sentences.zh: 會驚，謂維曰：「兵來似欲作惡，當云何？」

translations.literal: Hui was alarmed and said to Wei, "The troops seem to be coming to do evil—what should be done?"
translations.idiomatic: Hui was alarmed and said to Wei, "The troops seem to be coming to revolt—what should be done?"

sentences.zh: 維曰：「但當擊之耳！」

translations.literal: Wei said, "Just strike them!"
translations.idiomatic: Wei said, "Just strike them!"

sentences.zh: 會遣兵悉殺所閉諸牙門郡守，內人共舉機以拄門，兵斫門，不能破。

translations.literal: Hui dispatched troops to kill all the confined gate commanders and commandery governors; those inside together raised machines to brace the gate—the troops hacked at the gate but could not break it.
translations.idiomatic: Hui dispatched troops to kill all the confined gate commanders and commandery governors. Those inside together raised machines to brace the gate. The troops hacked at the gate but could not break it.

sentences.zh: 斯須，城外倚梯登城，或燒城屋，蟻附亂進，矢下如雨，牙門郡守各緣屋出，與其軍士相得。

translations.literal: In a moment, outside the city they climbed ladders to scale the walls, or burned city buildings; swarming like ants they advanced in disorder, arrows falling like rain; the gate commanders and commandery governors each climbed out along the roofs and rejoined their soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: In a moment, outside the city they climbed ladders to scale the walls or burned city buildings. Swarming like ants they advanced in disorder, arrows falling like rain. The gate commanders and commandery governors each climbed out along the roofs and rejoined their soldiers.

sentences.zh: 姜維率會左右戰，手殺五六人，眾格斬維，爭前殺會。

translations.literal: Jiang Wei led Hui's attendants in battle, personally killing five or six men; the crowd hacked Wei to death and vied to be first to kill Hui.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Wei led Hui's attendants in battle, personally killing five or six men. The crowd hacked Wei to death and vied to be first to kill Hui.

sentences.zh: 會將士死者數百人，殺漢太子璿及姜維妻子，軍眾鈔略，死喪狼藉。

translations.literal: Several hundred of Hui's officers and soldiers died; the Shu crown prince Xuan and Jiang Wei's wife and children were killed; the army plundered and corpses lay scattered in disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Several hundred of Hui's officers and soldiers died. The Shu crown prince Liu Xuan and Jiang Wei's wife and children were killed. The army plundered and corpses lay scattered in disorder.

sentences.zh: 衛瓘部分諸將，數日乃定。

translations.literal: Wei Guan assigned the various generals; only after several days was order restored.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Guan assigned the various generals. Only after several days was order restored.

sentences.zh: 鄧艾本營將士追出艾於檻車，迎還。

translations.literal: The officers and soldiers of Deng Ai's original camp pursued and brought Ai out of the caged cart, welcoming him back.
translations.idiomatic: The officers and soldiers of Deng Ai's original camp pursued and brought Ai out of the caged cart, welcoming him back.

sentences.zh: 衛瓘自以與會共陷艾，恐其為變，乃遣護軍田續等將兵襲艾，遇於綿竹西，斬艾父子。

translations.literal: Wei Guan, thinking that he and Hui had together framed Ai, feared Ai would cause trouble; he therefore dispatched Protector of the Army Tian Xu and others to lead troops and attack Ai; they met west of Mianzhu and beheaded Ai and his son.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Guan, thinking that he and Hui had together framed Ai, feared Ai would cause trouble. He therefore dispatched Protector of the Army Tian Xu and others to attack Ai. They met west of Mianzhu and beheaded Ai and his son.

sentences.zh: 艾之入江油也，田續不進，艾欲斬續，既而捨之。

translations.literal: When Ai entered Jiangyou, Tian Xu did not advance; Ai wished to execute Xu but afterward spared him.
translations.idiomatic: When Ai entered Jiangyou, Tian Xu did not advance. Ai wished to execute Xu but afterward spared him.

sentences.zh: 及瓘遣續，謂曰：「可以報江油之辱矣。」

translations.literal: When Guan dispatched Xu, he said to him, "You can now avenge the humiliation at Jiangyou."
translations.idiomatic: When Guan dispatched Xu, he said to him, "You can now avenge the humiliation at Jiangyou."

sentences.zh: 鎮西長史杜預言於眾曰：「伯玉其不免乎？

translations.literal: Chief Clerk Du Yu of the Army of the West said to the assembly, "Will Boyu not escape disaster?
translations.idiomatic: Chief Clerk Du Yu of the Army of the West said to the assembly, "Will Boyu not escape disaster?

sentences.zh: 身為名士，位望已高，既無德音，又不御下以正，將何以堪其責乎！」

translations.literal: As a famous gentleman his position and prestige are already high; he has neither virtuous reputation nor governs subordinates with rectitude—how can he bear his responsibility!"
translations.idiomatic: As a famous gentleman his position and prestige are already high. He has neither virtuous reputation nor governs subordinates with rectitude. How can he bear his responsibility!"

sentences.zh: 瓘聞之，不候駕而謝預。

translations.literal: Guan heard this and, without waiting for the imperial carriage, went to apologize to Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Guan heard this and, without waiting for the imperial carriage, went to apologize to Yu.

sentences.zh: 預，恕之子也。

translations.literal: Yu was the son of Du Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Du Yu was the son of Du Shu.

sentences.zh: 鄧艾餘子在洛陽者悉伏誅。

translations.literal: All of Deng Ai's remaining sons in Luoyang were executed.
translations.idiomatic: All of Deng Ai's remaining sons in Luoyang were executed.

sentences.zh: 徙其妻及孫於西城。

translations.literal: His wife and grandson were relocated to the western city.
translations.idiomatic: His wife and grandson were relocated to the western city.

sentences.zh: 鐘會兄毓嘗密言於晉公曰：「會挾術難保，不可專任。」

translations.literal: Zhong Hui's elder brother Yu once secretly said to the Duke of Jin, "Hui relies on his skill and is hard to keep safe—he cannot be solely entrusted."
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Hui's elder brother Zhong Yu once secretly said to the Duke of Jin, "Hui relies on his skill and is hard to keep safe. He cannot be solely entrusted."

sentences.zh: 及會反，毓已卒，晉公思鐘繇之勳與毓之賢，特原毓子峻、迪，官爵如故。

translations.literal: When Hui rebelled, Yu had already died; the Duke of Jin, thinking of Zhong Yao's merit and Yu's worth, specially pardoned Yu's sons Jun and Di, their offices and titles as before.
translations.idiomatic: When Hui rebelled, Yu had already died. The Duke of Jin, thinking of Zhong Yao's merit and Yu's worth, specially pardoned Yu's sons Jun and Di, their offices and titles as before.

sentences.zh: 會功曹向雄收葬會屍，晉公召而責之曰：「往者王經之死，卿哭於東市而我不問；

translations.literal: Hui's Merit Officer Xiang Xiong collected and buried Hui's corpse; the Duke of Jin summoned and rebuked him, saying, "Formerly at Wang Jing's death you wept at the eastern market and I did not inquire;
translations.idiomatic: Hui's Merit Officer Xiang Xiong collected and buried Hui's corpse. The Duke of Jin summoned and rebuked him, saying, "Formerly at Wang Jing's death you wept at the eastern market and I did not inquire.

sentences.zh: 鐘會躬為叛逆，又輒收葬，若復相容，當如王法何！」

translations.literal: Zhong Hui personally committed rebellion, yet you again collected and buried him—if I again tolerate this, what of royal law!"
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Hui personally committed rebellion, yet you again collected and buried him. If I again tolerate this, what of royal law!"

sentences.zh: 雄曰：「昔先王掩骼埋胔，仁流朽骨，當時豈先卜其功罪而後收葬哉！

translations.literal: Xiong said, "Formerly the ancient kings covered exposed bones and buried scattered flesh—benevolence flowed to decayed bones; did they first divined merit and crime before collecting burial!
translations.idiomatic: Xiong said, "Formerly the ancient kings covered exposed bones and buried scattered flesh—benevolence flowed even to decayed bones. Did they first divined merit and crime before collecting burial!

sentences.zh: 今王誅既加，於法已備；

translations.literal: Now the royal punishment has been applied and the law is complete;
translations.idiomatic: Now the royal punishment has been applied and the law is complete.

sentences.zh: 雄感義收葬，教亦無闕。

translations.literal: Xiong, moved by righteousness, collected burial—teaching also lacks nothing.
translations.idiomatic: I, moved by righteousness, collected burial—teaching also lacks nothing.

sentences.zh: 法立於上，教弘於下，以此訓物，不亦可乎？

translations.literal: Law is established above, teaching spread below—to instruct the people thus, is it not acceptable?
translations.idiomatic: Law is established above, teaching spread below. To instruct the people thus—is it not acceptable?

sentences.zh: 何必使雄背死違生，以立於世！

translations.literal: Why must you make Xiong turn his back on the dead and violate life to stand in the world!
translations.idiomatic: Why must you make me turn my back on the dead and violate life to stand in the world!

sentences.zh: 明公讎懟枯骨，捐之中野，豈仁賢之度哉！」

translations.literal: Your Excellency would take vengeance on dry bones and cast them in the wild— is this the measure of the benevolent and worthy!"
translations.idiomatic: Your Excellency would take vengeance on dry bones and cast them in the wild—is this the measure of the benevolent and worthy!"

sentences.zh: 晉公悅，與宴談而遣之。

translations.literal: The Duke of Jin was pleased, feasted and talked with him, and sent him away.
translations.idiomatic: The Duke of Jin was pleased, feasted and talked with him, and sent him away.

sentences.zh: 二月，丙辰，車駕還洛陽。

translations.literal: In the second month, on day bingchen, the imperial carriage returned to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on the day bingchen, the imperial carriage returned to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 庚申，葬明元皇后。

translations.literal: On day gengshen, Empress Mingyuan was buried.
translations.idiomatic: On the day gengshen, Empress Mingyuan was buried.

sentences.zh: 初，劉禪使巴東太守襄陽羅憲將兵二千人守永安，聞成都敗，吏民驚擾，憲斬稱成都亂者一人，百姓乃定。

translations.literal: At the outset, Liu Shan had Luo Xian of Xiangyang, Governor of Badong, lead two thousand troops to guard Yong'an; hearing that Chengdu had fallen, officials and people were alarmed and disturbed; Xian beheaded one who claimed Chengdu was in chaos, and the people then settled.
translations.idiomatic: At the outset, Liu Shan had Luo Xian of Xiangyang, Governor of Badong, lead two thousand troops to guard Yong'an. Hearing that Chengdu had fallen, officials and people were alarmed and disturbed. Xian beheaded one who claimed Chengdu was in chaos, and the people then settled.

sentences.zh: 及得禪手敕，乃帥所統臨於都亭三日。

translations.literal: When he received Shan's handwritten edict, he then led his command to mourn at the capital pavilion for three days.
translations.idiomatic: When he received Shan's handwritten edict, he then led his command to mourn at the capital pavilion for three days.

sentences.zh: 吳聞蜀敗，起兵西上，外托救援，內欲襲憲。

translations.literal: Wu heard Shu had fallen and raised troops westward; outwardly claiming rescue, inwardly wishing to attack Xian.
translations.idiomatic: Wu heard Shu had fallen and raised troops westward, outwardly claiming rescue but inwardly wishing to attack Xian.

sentences.zh: 憲曰：「本朝傾覆，吳為脣齒，不恤我難而背盟徼利，不義甚矣。

translations.literal: Xian said, "Our dynasty has fallen; Wu is lip and teeth to us—yet they do not pity our hardship but break alliance to seek profit—this is greatly unrighteous.
translations.idiomatic: Xian said, "Our dynasty has fallen. Wu is lip and teeth to us, yet they do not pity our hardship but break alliance to seek profit. This is greatly unrighteous.

sentences.zh: 且漢已亡，吳何得久？

translations.literal: Moreover, Han is already perished—how can Wu long endure?
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, Han is already perished. How can Wu long endure?

sentences.zh: 我寧能為吳降虜乎！」

translations.literal: How could I become a surrendered captive of Wu!"
translations.idiomatic: How could I become a surrendered captive of Wu!"

sentences.zh: 保城繕甲，告誓將士，厲以節義，莫不憤激。

translations.literal: He defended the city and repaired armor, addressed and swore the officers and soldiers, urging them with integrity and righteousness—all were stirred with indignation.
translations.idiomatic: He defended the city and repaired armor, addressed and swore the officers and soldiers, urging them with integrity and righteousness. All were stirred with indignation.

sentences.zh: 吳人聞鐘、鄧敗，百城無主，有兼蜀之志，而巴東固守，兵不得過，乃使撫軍步協率眾而西。

translations.literal: The people of Wu heard that Zhong and Deng were defeated, a hundred cities had no master, and they had ambition to annex Shu; but Badong held firm and troops could not pass—they therefore sent Pacifying General Bu Xie to lead the host westward.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Wu heard that Zhong and Deng were defeated and a hundred cities had no master. They had ambition to annex Shu, but Badong held firm and troops could not pass. They therefore sent Pacifying General Bu Xie to lead the host westward.

sentences.zh: 憲力弱不能御，遣參軍楊宗突圍北出，告急於安東將軍陳騫，又送文武印綬、任子詣晉公。

translations.literal: Xian's strength was weak and he could not resist; he dispatched Aide Yang Zong to break out north and report urgency to General Who Pacifies the East Chen Qian, and also sent civil and military seals and cords and a hostage son to the Duke of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Xian's strength was weak and he could not resist. He dispatched Aide Yang Zong to break out north and report urgency to General Who Pacifies the East Chen Qian, and also sent civil and military seals and cords and a hostage son to the Duke of Jin.

sentences.zh: 協攻永安，憲與戰，大破之。

translations.literal: Xie attacked Yong'an; Xian fought him and inflicted a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Xie attacked Yong'an. Xian fought him and inflicted a great defeat.

sentences.zh: 吳主怒，復遣鎮軍陸抗等帥眾三萬人增憲之圍。

translations.literal: The Lord of Wu was enraged and again dispatched General Who Guards the Army Lu Kang and others to lead thirty thousand troops to reinforce the siege of Xian.
translations.idiomatic: The Wu ruler was enraged and again dispatched General Who Guards the Army Lu Kang and others to lead thirty thousand troops to reinforce the siege of Xian.

sentences.zh: 三月，丁丑，以司空王祥為太尉，征北將軍何曾為司徒，左僕射荀顗為司空。

translations.literal: In the third month, on day dingchou, Minister of Works Wang Xiang was made Grand Commandant, General Who Conquers the North He Zeng was made Minister over the Masses, and Left Deputy Director Xun Yi was made Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on the day dingchou, Minister of Works Wang Xiang was made Grand Commandant, General Who Conquers the North He Zeng was made Minister over the Masses, and Left Deputy Director Xun Yi was made Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 己卯，進晉公爵為王，增封十郡。

translations.literal: On day jimao, the Duke of Jin was advanced to King and his fief increased by ten commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: On the day jimao, the Duke of Jin was advanced to King and his fief was increased by ten commanderies.

sentences.zh: 王祥、何曾、荀顗共詣晉王，顗謂祥曰：「相王尊重，何侯與一朝之臣皆已盡敬，今日便當相率而拜，無所疑也。」

translations.literal: Wang Xiang, He Zeng, and Xun Yi together went to the King of Jin; Yi said to Xiang, "The Chancellor-King is honored; Lord He and the ministers of the court have all shown full respect—today we should lead one another in bowing, with no doubt."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xiang, He Zeng, and Xun Yi together went to the King of Jin. Yi said to Xiang, "The Chancellor-King is honored. Lord He and the ministers of the court have all shown full respect. Today we should lead one another in bowing, with no doubt."

sentences.zh: 祥曰：「相國雖尊，要是魏之宰相，吾等魏之三公，王、公相去一階而已，安有天子三公可輒拜人者！

translations.literal: Xiang said, "Although the Chancellor is honored, after all he is Wei's chancellor; we are Wei's Three Dukes—king and duke differ by one rank—how can the Three Dukes of the Son of Heaven casually bow to another!
translations.idiomatic: Xiang said, "Although the Chancellor is honored, after all he is Wei's chancellor. We are Wei's Three Dukes—king and duke differ by one rank. How can the Three Dukes of the Son of Heaven casually bow to another!

sentences.zh: 損魏朝之望，虧晉王之德，君子愛人以禮，我不為也。」

translations.literal: It would harm the Wei court's dignity and diminish the Jin King's virtue—the gentleman loves people through ritual; I will not do it."
translations.idiomatic: It would harm the Wei court's dignity and diminish the Jin King's virtue. The gentleman loves people through ritual. I will not do it."

sentences.zh: 及入，顗遂拜，而祥獨長揖。

translations.literal: When they entered, Yi then bowed, but Xiang alone made a long bow with hands clasped.
translations.idiomatic: When they entered, Yi bowed, but Xiang alone made a long bow with hands clasped.

sentences.zh: 王謂祥曰：「今日然後知君見顧之重也！」

translations.literal: The King said to Xiang, "Only today do I know the weight of your regard for me!"
translations.idiomatic: The King said to Xiang, "Only today do I know the weight of your regard for me!"

sentences.zh: 劉禪舉家東遷洛陽，時擾攘倉卒，禪之大臣無從行者，惟秘書令郤正及殿中督汝南張通捨妻子單身隨禪，禪賴正相導宜適，舉動無闕，乃慨然歎息，恨知正之晚。

translations.literal: Liu Shan moved his whole household east to Luoyang; at the time of turmoil and haste, none of Shan's great ministers accompanied him—only Secretariat Director Xi Zheng and Palace Supervisor Zhang Tong of Runan abandoned wife and children and followed Shan alone; Shan relied on Zheng to guide what was fitting, his conduct without fault, and sighed with emotion, regretting he had known Zheng too late.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Shan moved his whole household east to Luoyang. In the turmoil and haste, none of Shan's great ministers accompanied him. Only Secretariat Director Xi Zheng and Palace Supervisor Zhang Tong of Runan abandoned wife and children and followed Shan alone. Shan relied on Zheng to guide what was fitting, his conduct without fault, and sighed with emotion, regretting he had known Zheng too late.

sentences.zh: 初，漢建棕太守霍弋都督南中，聞魏兵至，欲赴成都，劉禪以備敵既定，不聽。

translations.literal: At the outset, Huo Yi, Governor of Jianning, supervised the south; hearing Wei troops had arrived, he wished to go to Chengdu; Liu Shan, because defense against the enemy was already settled, would not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: At the outset, Huo Yi, Governor of Jianning, supervised the south. Hearing Wei troops had arrived, he wished to go to Chengdu. Liu Shan, because defense against the enemy was already settled, would not permit it.

sentences.zh: 成都不守，弋素服大臨三日。

translations.literal: When Chengdu was not held, Yi wore plain garb and mourned greatly for three days.
translations.idiomatic: When Chengdu fell, Yi wore plain garb and mourned greatly for three days.

sentences.zh: 諸將咸勸弋宜速降，弋曰：「今道路隔塞，未詳主之安危，去就大故，不可苟也。

translations.literal: The generals all urged Yi to surrender quickly; Yi said, "Now the roads are blocked and cut off, the lord's safety or peril is not clear—going or staying is a great matter and cannot be done rashly.
translations.idiomatic: The generals all urged Yi to surrender quickly. Yi said, "Now the roads are blocked and cut off, and the lord's safety or peril is not clear. Going or staying is a great matter and cannot be done rashly.

sentences.zh: 若魏以禮遇主上，則保境而降不晚也。

translations.literal: If Wei treats our lord with courtesy, then holding the territory and surrendering will not be too late.
translations.idiomatic: If Wei treats our lord with courtesy, then holding the territory and surrendering will not be too late.

sentences.zh: 若萬一危辱，吾將以死拒之，何論遲速邪！」

translations.literal: If by chance there is danger and humiliation, I will resist with death—what talk of early or late!"
translations.idiomatic: If by chance there is danger and humiliation, I will resist with death. What talk of early or late!"

sentences.zh: 得禪東遷之問，始率六郡將守上表曰：「臣聞人生在三，事之如一，惟難所在，則致其命。

translations.literal: When he received news of Shan's eastward move, he then led the generals and defenders of six commanderies to submit a memorial, saying, "Your subject has heard that in life one serves three lords as one—wherever difficulty lies, one gives one's life.
translations.idiomatic: When he received news of Shan's eastward move, he then led the generals and defenders of six commanderies to submit a memorial, saying, "Your subject has heard that in life one serves three lords as one—wherever difficulty lies, one gives one's life.

sentences.zh: 今臣國敗主附，守死無所，是以委質，不敢有貳。」

translations.literal: Now my state is defeated and my lord has submitted; to hold and die has no place—therefore I submit my person and dare not have two hearts."
translations.idiomatic: Now my state is defeated and my lord has submitted. To hold and die has no place. Therefore I submit my person and dare not have two hearts."

sentences.zh: 晉王善之，拜南中都尉，委以本任。

translations.literal: The King of Jin approved, appointed him Commandant of the Southern Center, and entrusted him with his original duties.
translations.idiomatic: The King of Jin approved, appointed him Commandant of the Southern Center, and entrusted him with his original duties.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，封劉禪為安樂公，子孫及群臣封侯者五十餘人。

translations.literal: On day dinghai, Liu Shan was enfeoffed as Duke of Anle; his descendants and more than fifty ministers were enfeoffed as marquises.
translations.idiomatic: On the day dinghai, Liu Shan was enfeoffed as Duke of Anle. His descendants and more than fifty ministers were enfeoffed as marquises.

sentences.zh: 晉王與禪宴，為之作故蜀伎，旁人皆為之感愴，而禪喜笑自若。

translations.literal: The King of Jin feasted with Shan and had former Shu performers play for him; those nearby were all moved to sorrow, yet Shan smiled and laughed as if at ease.
translations.idiomatic: The King of Jin feasted with Shan and had former Shu performers play for him. Those nearby were all moved to sorrow, yet Shan smiled and laughed as if at ease.

sentences.zh: 王謂賈充曰：「人之無情，乃至於是！

translations.literal: The King said to Jia Chong, "Human heartlessness reaches even to this!
translations.idiomatic: The King said to Jia Chong, "Human heartlessness reaches even to this!

sentences.zh: 雖使諸葛亮在，不能輔之久全，況姜維邪！」

translations.literal: Even if Zhuge Liang were present, he could not help him long endure—how much less Jiang Wei!"
translations.idiomatic: Even if Zhuge Liang were present, he could not help him long endure—how much less Jiang Wei!"

sentences.zh: 他日，王問禪曰：「頗思蜀否？」

translations.literal: Another day the King asked Shan, "Do you rather miss Shu?"
translations.idiomatic: Another day the King asked Shan, "Do you miss Shu?"

sentences.zh: 禪曰：「此間樂，不思蜀也。」

translations.literal: Shan said, "Here is happiness—I do not think of Shu."
translations.idiomatic: Shan said, "Here is happiness. I do not think of Shu."

sentences.zh: 郤正聞之，謂禪曰：「若正後問，宜泣而答：『先人墳墓，遠在岷、蜀，乃心西悲，無日不思。」

translations.literal: Xi Zheng heard this and said to Shan, "If he asks again later, you should weep and answer: 'My forefathers' tombs are far away in Min and Shu; my heart grieves westward—there is no day I do not think of them.'"
translations.idiomatic: Xi Zheng heard this and said to Shan, "If he asks again later, you should weep and answer: 'My forefathers' tombs are far away in Min and Shu. My heart grieves westward—there is no day I do not think of them.'"

sentences.zh: 因閉其目。」

translations.literal: He then closed his eyes.
translations.idiomatic: He then closed his eyes.

sentences.zh: 會王復問，祥對如前，王曰：「何乃似郤正語邪！」

translations.literal: When the King again asked, Xiang answered as before; the King said, "Why does it sound like Xi Zheng's words!"
translations.idiomatic: When the King again asked, Shan answered as before. The King said, "Why does it sound like Xi Zheng's words!"

sentences.zh: 禪驚視曰：「誠如尊命。」

translations.literal: Shan looked up in alarm and said, "It is truly as Your Excellency says."
translations.idiomatic: Shan looked up in alarm and said, "It is truly as Your Excellency says."

sentences.zh: 左右皆笑。

translations.literal: Those nearby all laughed.
translations.idiomatic: Those nearby all laughed.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，新附督王稚浮海入吳句章，略其長吏及男女二百餘口而還。

translations.literal: In summer, fourth month, Supervisor of Newly Submitted Wang Zhi crossed the sea into Wu's Jukou, plundered its chief officials and more than two hundred men and women, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, in the fourth month, Supervisor of Newly Submitted Wang Zhi crossed the sea into Wu's Jukou, plundered its chief officials and more than two hundred men and women, and returned.

sentences.zh: 五月，庚申，晉王奏復五等爵，封騎督以上六百餘人。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on day gengshen, the King of Jin memorialized to restore the five ranks of nobility and enfeoffed more than six hundred cavalry commanders and above.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on the day gengshen, the King of Jin memorialized to restore the five ranks of nobility and enfeoffed more than six hundred cavalry commanders and above.

sentences.zh: 甲戌，改元。

translations.literal: On day jiaxu, the reign era was changed.
translations.idiomatic: On the day jiaxu, the reign era was changed.

sentences.zh: 癸未，追命舞陽主理侯懿為晉宣王，忠武侯師為景王。

translations.literal: On day guiwei, posthumous orders were issued appointing Marquis Zhuili of Wuyang Yi as King Xuan of Jin and Marquis Zhongwu Shi as King Jing.
translations.idiomatic: On the day guiwei, posthumous orders were issued appointing Marquis Zhuili of Wuyang Sima Yi as King Xuan of Jin and Marquis Zhongwu Sima Shi as King Jing.

sentences.zh: 羅憲被攻凡六月，救援不到，城中疾病太半。

translations.literal: Luo Xian was under attack for six months in all; relief did not arrive, and more than half in the city were sick.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Xian was under attack for six months in all. Relief did not arrive, and more than half in the city were sick.

sentences.zh: 或說憲棄城走，憲曰：「吾為城主，百姓所仰。

translations.literal: Some urged Xian to abandon the city and flee; Xian said, "I am master of the city—the people rely on me.
translations.idiomatic: Some urged Xian to abandon the city and flee. Xian said, "I am master of the city—the people rely on me.

sentences.zh: 危不能安，急而棄之，君子不為也，畢命於此矣！」

translations.literal: In peril I cannot bring safety; in urgency I abandon them—a gentleman does not do this; I will give my life here!"
translations.idiomatic: In peril I cannot bring safety, and in urgency I would abandon them—a gentleman does not do this. I will give my life here!"

sentences.zh: 陳騫言於晉王，遣荊州刺史胡烈將步騎二萬攻西陵以救憲。

translations.literal: Chen Qian spoke to the King of Jin, who dispatched Inspector of Jing Province Hu Lie to lead twenty thousand foot and horse to attack Xiling and rescue Xian.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Qian spoke to the King of Jin, who dispatched Inspector of Jing Province Hu Lie to lead twenty thousand foot and horse to attack Xiling and rescue Xian.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，吳師退。

translations.literal: In autumn, seventh month, Wu troops withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, in the seventh month, Wu troops withdrew.

sentences.zh: 晉王使憲因仍舊任，加陵江將軍，封萬年亭侯。

translations.literal: The King of Jin had Xian continue in his original post, added General Who Crosses the River, and enfeoffed him as Marquis of Wannian District.
translations.idiomatic: The King of Jin had Xian continue in his original post, added the title General Who Crosses the River, and enfeoffed him as Marquis of Wannian District.

sentences.zh: 晉王奏使司空荀顗定禮儀，中護軍賈充正法律，尚書僕射裴秀議官制，太保鄭沖總而裁焉。

translations.literal: The King of Jin memorialized to have Minister of Works Xun Yi fix ritual and ceremony, Central Protector of the Army Jia Chong rectify laws, Deputy Director of the Secretariat Pei Xiu discuss the official system, and Grand Tutor Zheng Chong oversee and decide all.
translations.idiomatic: The King of Jin memorialized to have Minister of Works Xun Yi fix ritual and ceremony, Central Protector of the Army Jia Chong rectify laws, Deputy Director of the Secretariat Pei Xiu discuss the official system, and Grand Tutor Zheng Chong oversee and decide all.

sentences.zh: 吳分交州置廣州。

translations.literal: Wu divided Jiaozhou to establish Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wu divided Jiaozhou to establish Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 吳主寢疾，口不能言，乃手書呼丞相濮陽興入，令子□出拜之。

translations.literal: The Lord of Wu lay ill in bed and could not speak; he therefore wrote by hand summoning Chancellor Puyang Xing to enter and ordered his son □ to come out and bow to him.
translations.idiomatic: The Wu ruler lay gravely ill and could not speak. He therefore wrote by hand summoning Chancellor Puyang Xing to enter and ordered his son to come out and bow to him.

sentences.zh: 休把興臂，把□以托之。

translations.literal: Xiu took Xing's arm and took □ to entrust him.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Xiu took Xing's arm and placed his heir in Xing's hands to entrust him.

sentences.zh: 癸未，吳主殂，謚曰景帝。

translations.literal: On day guiwei, the Lord of Wu died; his posthumous title was Emperor Jing.
translations.idiomatic: On the day guiwei, the Wu ruler died. His posthumous title was Emperor Jing.

sentences.zh: 群臣尊朱皇后為皇太后。

translations.literal: The ministers honored Empress Zhu as Empress Dowager.
translations.idiomatic: The ministers honored Empress Zhu as Empress Dowager.

sentences.zh: 吳人以蜀初亡，交趾攜叛，國內恐懼，欲得長君。

translations.literal: The people of Wu, because Shu had just perished and Jiaozhi had rebelled in succession, were fearful within the state and wished to obtain an elder ruler.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Wu, because Shu had just fallen and Jiaozhi had rebelled in succession, were fearful within the state and wished to obtain an elder ruler.

sentences.zh: 左典軍萬嘗為烏程令，與烏程侯皓相善，稱「皓才識明斷，長沙桓王之儔也；

translations.literal: Left Palace Army Commander Wan, who had been magistrate of Wucheng, was on good terms with Marquis of Wucheng Hao, and praised him, saying, "Hao's talent and judgment are clear and decisive—he is a match for the King of Changsha Huan;
translations.idiomatic: Left Palace Army Commander Wan, who had been magistrate of Wucheng, was on good terms with Marquis of Wucheng Sun Hao and praised him, saying, "Hao's talent and judgment are clear and decisive—he is a match for the King of Changsha Sun Huan.

sentences.zh: 又加之好學，奉遵法度。」

translations.literal: Moreover he loves learning and observes and follows law and regulation."
translations.idiomatic: Moreover he loves learning and observes law and regulation."

sentences.zh: 屢言之於丞相興、左將軍布，興、布說朱太后，欲以皓為嗣。

translations.literal: He repeatedly spoke of this to Chancellor Xing and Left General Bu; Xing and Bu persuaded Empress Zhu and wished to make Hao the heir.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly spoke of this to Chancellor Xing and Left General Bu. Xing and Bu persuaded Empress Zhu and wished to make Hao the heir.

sentences.zh: 朱後曰：「我寡婦人，安知社稷之慮，苟吳國無隕，宗廟有賴，可矣。」

translations.literal: Empress Zhu said, "I am a widow—how would I know the concerns of the altars of soil and grain? If only Wu does not fall and the ancestral temple has reliance, that is enough."
translations.idiomatic: Empress Zhu said, "I am a widow—how would I know the concerns of state? If only Wu does not fall and the ancestral temple has someone to rely on, that is enough."

sentences.zh: 於是遂迎立皓，改元元興，大赦。

translations.literal: Thereupon they welcomed and established Hao, changed the era name to Yuanxing, and proclaimed a general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon they welcomed and established Sun Hao, changed the era name to Yuanxing, and proclaimed a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 八月，庚寅，命中撫軍司馬炎副貳相國事。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on day gengyin, Central Pacifying Army Major Sima Yan was ordered to assist in the Chancellor's affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on the day gengyin, Central Pacifying Army Major Sima Yan was ordered to assist in the Chancellor's affairs.

sentences.zh: 初，鐘會之伐漢也，辛憲英謂其夫之從子羊祜曰：「會在事縱恣，非持久處下之道，吾畏其有他志也。」

translations.literal: At the outset, when Zhong Hui attacked Han, Xin Xianying said to her husband's nephew Yang Hu, "Hui in affairs is willful and unrestrained—not a way to long remain in subordinate position; I fear he has other intentions."
translations.idiomatic: At the outset, when Zhong Hui attacked Shu, Xin Xianying said to her husband's nephew Yang Hu, "Hui in affairs is willful and unrestrained—not a way to long remain in subordinate position. I fear he has other intentions."

sentences.zh: 會請其子郎中琇為參軍，憲英憂曰：「他日吾為國憂，今日難至吾家矣。」

translations.literal: Hui requested her son Attendant Gentleman Xiu as military adviser; Xianying worried, saying, "Formerly I worried for the state; today disaster has reached my own house."
translations.idiomatic: Hui requested her son Attendant Gentleman Yang Xiu as military adviser. Xianying worried, saying, "Formerly I worried for the state. Today disaster has reached my own house."

sentences.zh: 琇固請於晉王，王不聽。

translations.literal: Xiu firmly petitioned the King of Jin, but the King would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Xiu firmly petitioned the King of Jin, but the King would not listen.

sentences.zh: 憲英謂琇曰：「行矣，戒之，軍旅之間，可以濟者，其惟仁恕乎！」

translations.literal: Xianying said to Xiu, "Go; be warned—in the midst of armies, what can save you is perhaps only benevolence and forbearance!"
translations.idiomatic: Xianying said to Xiu, "Go, and be warned. In the midst of armies, what can save you is perhaps only benevolence and forbearance!"

sentences.zh: 琇竟以全歸。

translations.literal: Xiu ultimately returned safely.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Xiu ultimately returned safely.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，詔以琇嘗諫會反，賜爵關內侯。

translations.literal: On day guisi, an edict, because Xiu had once remonstrated against Hui's rebellion, granted him the title Marquis Within the Passes.
translations.idiomatic: On the day guisi, an edict, because Yang Xiu had once remonstrated against Hui's rebellion, granted him the title Marquis Within the Passes.

sentences.zh: 九月，戊午，以司馬炎為撫軍大將軍。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on day wuwu, Sima Yan was made Grand General Who Pacifies the Army.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on the day wuwu, Sima Yan was made Grand General Who Pacifies the Army.

sentences.zh: 辛未，詔以呂興為安南將軍，都督交州諸軍事，以南中監軍霍弋遙領交州刺史，得以便宜選用長吏。

translations.literal: On day xinwei, an edict made Lü Xing General Who Pacifies the South and supervisor of Jiaozhou military affairs; Supervisor of the Southern Center Huo Yi was remotely appointed Inspector of Jiaozhou and authorized to select chief officials as expedience required.
translations.idiomatic: On the day xinwei, an edict made Lü Xing General Who Pacifies the South and supervisor of Jiaozhou military affairs. Supervisor of the Southern Center Huo Yi was remotely appointed Inspector of Jiaozhou and authorized to select chief officials as expedience required.

sentences.zh: 弋表遣建寧爨谷為交趾太守，率牙門董元、毛炅、孟幹、孟通、爨能、李松、王素等將兵助興。

translations.literal: Yi memorialized dispatching Cuan Gu of Jianning as Governor of Jiaozhi, leading gate officers Dong Yuan, Mao Jiong, Meng Gan, Meng Tong, Cuan Neng, Li Song, Wang Su, and others to lead troops to aid Xing.
translations.idiomatic: Yi memorialized dispatching Cuan Gu of Jianning as Governor of Jiaozhi, leading gate officers Dong Yuan, Mao Jiong, Meng Gan, Meng Tong, Cuan Neng, Li Song, Wang Su, and others to lead troops to aid Xing.

sentences.zh: 未至，興為其功曹李統所殺。

translations.literal: Before they arrived, Xing was killed by his Merit Officer Li Tong.
translations.idiomatic: Before they arrived, Xing was killed by his Merit Officer Li Tong.

sentences.zh: 吳主貶朱太后為景皇后，追謚父和曰文皇帝，尊母何氏為太后。

translations.literal: The Lord of Wu demoted Empress Zhu to Empress Jing, posthumously titled his father He as Emperor Wen, and honored his mother Lady He as Empress Dowager.
translations.idiomatic: The Wu ruler demoted Empress Zhu to Empress Jing, posthumously titled his father Sun He as Emperor Wen, and honored his mother Lady He as Empress Dowager.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，丁亥，詔以壽春所獲吳相國參軍事徐紹為散騎常侍，水曹掾孫彧為給事黃門侍郎，以使於吳，其家人在此者悉聽自隨，不必使還，以開廣大信。

translations.literal: In winter, tenth month, on day dinghai, an edict appointed Xu Shao, military adviser to Wu's Chancellor captured at Shouchun, as Regular Attendant of the Dispersed Cavalry, and Sun Yu, clerk of the Water Bureau, as Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate, to serve as envoys to Wu; their families here were all permitted to follow of their own accord and need not be sent back—to open broad trust.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, in the tenth month, on the day dinghai, an edict appointed Xu Shao, military adviser to Wu's Chancellor captured at Shouchun, as Regular Attendant of the Dispersed Cavalry, and Sun Yu, clerk of the Water Bureau, as Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate, to serve as envoys to Wu. Their families here were all permitted to follow of their own accord and need not be sent back, to open broad trust.

sentences.zh: 晉王因政書吳主，諭以禍福。

translations.literal: The King of Jin therefore sent a letter to the Lord of Wu, instructing him on fortune and disaster.
translations.idiomatic: The King of Jin therefore sent a letter to the Wu ruler, instructing him on fortune and disaster.

sentences.zh: 初，晉王娶王肅之女，生炎及攸，以攸繼景王后。

translations.literal: At the outset, the King of Jin married the daughter of Wang Su and begot Yan and You; he had You succeed the King Jing.
translations.idiomatic: At the outset, the King of Jin married the daughter of Wang Su and begot Yan and You. He had You succeed King Jing.

sentences.zh: 攸性孝友，多材藝，清和平允，名聞過於炎。

translations.literal: You was filial and friendly by nature, had many talents and skills, was pure, harmonious, and even-handed, and his fame exceeded Yan's.
translations.idiomatic: You was filial and friendly by nature, had many talents and skills, was pure, harmonious, and even-handed, and his fame exceeded Yan's.

sentences.zh: 晉王愛之，常曰：「天下者，景王之天下也，吾攝居相位，百年之後，大業宜歸攸。」

translations.literal: The King of Jin loved him and often said, "The realm is King Jing's realm; I hold the chancellorship in his stead—after a hundred years the great enterprise should go to You."
translations.idiomatic: The King of Jin loved him and often said, "The realm is King Jing's realm. I hold the chancellorship in his stead. After a hundred years the great enterprise should go to You."

sentences.zh: 炎立發委地，手垂過膝，嘗從容問裴秀曰：「人有相否？」

translations.literal: Yan stood with hair falling to the ground and hands hanging past the knees; he once casually asked Pei Xiu, "Do people have physiognomy?"
translations.idiomatic: Yan stood with hair falling to the ground and hands hanging past the knees. He once casually asked Pei Xiu, "Do people have physiognomy?"

sentences.zh: 因以異相示之。

translations.literal: He then showed him his unusual physiognomy.
translations.idiomatic: He then showed him his unusual physiognomy.

sentences.zh: 秀由是歸心。

translations.literal: From this Pei Xiu gave him his heart.
translations.idiomatic: From this Pei Xiu gave him his loyalty.

sentences.zh: 羊琇與炎善，為炎畫策，察時政所宜損益，皆令炎豫記之，以備晉王訪問。

translations.literal: Yang Xiu was on good terms with Yan and plotted strategy for him, observing what in current governance should be reduced or increased—all were had Yan record in advance to prepare for the King of Jin's inquiries.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Xiu was on good terms with Yan and plotted strategy for him, observing what in current governance should be reduced or increased. He had Yan record all of this in advance to prepare for the King of Jin's inquiries.

sentences.zh: 晉王欲以攸為世子，山濤曰：「廢長立少，違禮不祥。」

translations.literal: The King of Jin wished to make You heir apparent; Shan Tao said, "Deposing the elder and establishing the younger violates ritual and is inauspicious."
translations.idiomatic: The King of Jin wished to make You heir apparent. Shan Tao said, "Deposing the elder and establishing the younger violates ritual and is inauspicious."

sentences.zh: 賈充曰：「中撫軍有君人之德，不可易也。」

translations.literal: Jia Chong said, "The Central Pacifying Army commander has the virtue of a ruler—he cannot be replaced."
translations.idiomatic: Jia Chong said, "The Central Pacifying Army commander has the virtue of a ruler. He cannot be replaced."

sentences.zh: 何曾、裴秀曰：「中撫軍聰明神武，有超世之才，人望既茂，天表如此，固非人臣之相也。」

translations.literal: He Zeng and Pei Xiu said, "The Central Pacifying Army commander is bright, divine, and martial, with talent surpassing the age; human expectation is already abundant, and his heavenly countenance is such—this is truly not the physiognomy of a subject."
translations.idiomatic: He Zeng and Pei Xiu said, "The Central Pacifying Army commander is bright, divine, and martial, with talent surpassing the age. Human expectation is already abundant, and his heavenly countenance is such—this is truly not the physiognomy of a subject."

sentences.zh: 晉王由是意定，丙午，立炎為世子。

translations.literal: The King of Jin's mind was therefore settled; on day bingwu, Yan was established as heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: The King of Jin's mind was therefore settled. On the day bingwu, Yan was established as heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 吳主封太子□及其三弟皆為王，立妃滕氏為皇后。

translations.literal: The Lord of Wu enfeoffed the crown prince □ and his three younger brothers all as kings, and established Consort Teng as empress.
translations.idiomatic: The Wu ruler enfeoffed the crown prince and his three younger brothers all as kings, and established Consort Teng as empress.

sentences.zh: 初，吳主之立，發優詔，恤士民，開倉廩，振貧乏，科出宮女以配無妻者，禽獸養於苑中者皆放之。

translations.literal: At the outset, when the Lord of Wu was established, he issued gracious edicts, cared for gentry and people, opened granaries, relieved the poor, selected palace women to match with men without wives, and released all birds and beasts kept in the parks.
translations.idiomatic: At the outset, when the Wu ruler was established, he issued gracious edicts, cared for gentry and people, opened granaries, relieved the poor, selected palace women to match with men without wives, and released all birds and beasts kept in the parks.

sentences.zh: 當時翕然稱為明主。

translations.literal: At the time all harmoniously called him a wise ruler.
translations.idiomatic: At the time all harmoniously called him a wise ruler.

sentences.zh: 及既得志，粗暴矣盈，多忌諱，好酒色，大小失望，濮陽興、張布竊悔之。

translations.literal: When he had gotten his wish, brutality and arrogance overflowed; he had many taboos, loved wine and women; great and small were disappointed; Puyang Xing and Zhang Bu secretly regretted it.
translations.idiomatic: When he had gotten his wish, brutality and arrogance overflowed. He had many taboos and loved wine and women. Great and small were disappointed. Puyang Xing and Zhang Bu secretly regretted it.

sentences.zh: 或譖諸吳主，十一月，朔，興、布入朝，吳主執之，徙於廣州，道殺之，夷三族。

translations.literal: Some slandered them to the Lord of Wu; in the eleventh month, on the first day of the month, Xing and Bu entered court; the Lord of Wu seized them, exiled them to Guangzhou, killed them on the road, and exterminated three clans.
translations.idiomatic: Some slandered them to the Wu ruler. In the eleventh month, on the first day of the month, Xing and Bu entered court. The Wu ruler seized them, exiled them to Guangzhou, killed them on the road, and exterminated three clans.

sentences.zh: 以後父滕牧為衛將軍，錄尚書事。

translations.literal: The empress's father Teng Mu was made General of the Guard and recorded affairs of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: The empress's father Teng Mu was made General of the Guard and put in charge of Secretariat affairs.

sentences.zh: 牧，胤之族人也。

translations.literal: Mu was a clansman of Yin.
translations.idiomatic: Teng Mu was a clansman of Teng Yin.

sentences.zh: 是歲，罷屯田官。

translations.literal: This year the agricultural garrison officials were abolished.
translations.idiomatic: This year the agricultural garrison officials were abolished.
